Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 21, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Al-iqtirab (nearing, drawing close): it may be temporal or spatial. If the matter concerns distances, we say: "iqtaraba lil-nas hisabuhum" meaning its place. If it concerns time, we say: "iqtaraba zamanuh" (its time has drawn near). So al-iqtirab is the approach of an event to its container, whether time or place.

When the Almighty speaks in the past tense, saying ﴿Has drawn near﴾ (21:1), this indicates that the matter is binding and will certainly occur. Humans, when they speak of an approaching matter, say "yaqtarib" (is drawing near), not "iqtaraba" (has drawn near), because "iqtaraba" in this decisive form, judging that it has already happened, is said only by Allah, who owns events and has power over them. As for a human being, he does not own events, and he cannot pronounce judgment on something he does not possess once he utters this wording.

An example of this is His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ (16:1). "Atā" (has come) means that the matter occurred before He spoke, yet the matter is still in the future, as shown by His saying: ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾ (16:1). For one is only told "do not hasten something" if it has not yet happened. How, then, does He combine the past "atā" (has come) and the future "fa-la tasta'jilūhu" (so do not seek to hasten it)?

They said: You are forbidden to judge a future matter as past, because you do not own yourself, nor do you own the circumstances of the future, as in His saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," (23) unless [adding], "If Allah wills"﴾ (18:23–24).

You must attach this statement to the will of Allah, because your saying "I will do that tomorrow" is a proposition with its elements: the doer is you, the object is the act, the time is tomorrow, the cause that prompts you to act, and the power that enables you to act.

All these are elements over which you own nothing. Tomorrow may come and one of these elements may change, coming between you and what you want. Therefore you should clear yourself of the possibility of lying, so you say "in shā' Allāh" (if Allah wills) and refer the matter to the One who is able over it, who owns all these elements. It is as if your Lord is teaching you not to be a liar.

For this reason we find that the language has taken into account the capacity of the speaker and assigned him the appropriate tense. If you know that the action has occurred, say in the past: "Fulan has attended" — the matter is concluded. If you know that he has set out to attend and has prepared for it, say: "sa-yahḍuru Fulan" (Fulan will attend), meaning soon, or "sawfa yahḍuru" (he will attend), meaning later.

This suits the capacity of human beings. As for the Almighty, He owns the reins of things and their direction, and everything is subject to His creative command. If He says of a future matter "atā" (has come) or "iqtaraba" (has drawn near), it is true, because nothing takes the matter out of His intended will, and He alone has the power to be affected by the word "kun" (Be). When He utters it, the matter is concluded.

Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near﴾ (21:1), in the past form, and He did not say "yaqtarib" (is drawing near) or "sa-yaqtarib" (will draw near), because the speaker is Allah.

The past form "iqtaraba" also occurs in His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ (54:1).

And in His saying: ﴿Prostrate and draw near﴾ (96:19). "Iqtaraba" is not the same as "qaraba": "qaraba" means "dana" (came near), whereas "iqtaraba" means "dana jiddan" (came very near), until it becomes close to you.

Al-hisab (reckoning) is a word used in several senses. Al-hisab is to calculate a thing by numbers, by addition, subtraction, or multiplication, and to obtain a result in your favour or against you. If it is in your favour, you are a creditor; if it is against you, you are a debtor. Or it is to link causes to their effects.

There are matters that come without reckoning, as He said: ﴿Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ (3:37). This is a matter you cannot control, and Allah is not asked whether He gave an increase or a decrease.

As for "al-hisab" in ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near﴾ (21:1), it requires a reckoner, who is Allah, glorified and exalted; a party to be reckoned, who are the people; and a matter for which they are reckoned, which are the deeds and events they produced in their worldly life. These are of two kinds: a kind before they were obligated, and a kind after they were obligated.

As for what was before obligation and the age of puberty, Allah does not reckon us for it. Rather, He left us to frolic and roam in His blessings, without being asked about anything. But after puberty we are obligated to things that return good to us, and He binds us to the path that guarantees our happiness: "do" and "do not." This requires that we be reckoned, whether we did or did not act.

So the matter is reckoning, not arbitrary: a group in Paradise and a group in Hellfire. His saying, glorified is He, in the Hadith Qudsi: ("These are for Paradise and I do not mind; these are for the Fire and I do not mind")(1), is based on His knowledge of what they will perform at the time of reckoning. In Allah's knowledge is what they did and what they left undone.

Do not forget that the Reckoner in this situation is Allah. If the reckoning is for good, He deals with you with grace and increase as He wills, which is why He multiplies good deeds. If the reckoning is for evil, it is according to its measure without increase, as He said: ﴿A recompense in accordance [with their deeds]﴾ (78:26).

Since the Reckoner is Allah, glorified and exalted, and He gains nothing from what He decrees over creation, it is part of His mercy and grace toward us that He warned us of the causes of destruction, did not seize us unawares, and did not surprise us with reckoning unprepared. Rather, He explained the obligations to us, clarified the lawful and the unlawful, and informed us of the Day of Reckoning so that we might prepare for it, and not walk through life according to our whims.

So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ (99:7–8).

It is part of His mercy toward His servants that He promised them this promise and made known to them this balance while they were in abundance in the world, with the possibility of repairing mistakes and resuming repentance and righteous action. It is part of His mercy to us that He admonishes us with this admonition and repeats it to our ears night and day.

So our Lord did not seize us unawares, and the Resurrection did not surprise us with its terrors. Therefore, now know: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near﴾ (21:1). Since this is so, a person should consider how near the approach is, and when he will move on to the Day of Reckoning. Do not think that your lifespan is the lifespan of the world since Allah created it; rather, your lifespan and your world are according to the measure of your stay in it, and that stay is presumed, not certain. Some people live for ages, and some die in their mother's womb. So do not postpone, because you do not know whether the term will give you time to repent, or whether it will overtake you and you will be seized for your sin.

The Almighty says: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near﴾ (21:1), although the Hour is still far, and between us and the Resurrection is what only Allah knows. How is that?

They said: Because reckoning is only for deeds, and deeds have a time, which is the world. Whoever dies, his deeds have ended, and his reckoning has drawn near, because the period he spends in the grave he does not perceive, so it is like an hour of a day.

If you say: Some people live a hundred years, or a hundred and fifty years. We say: That is a presumption we do not guarantee, and a person is exposed to death at any moment, for a cause or without a cause.

We note in His saying: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near﴾ (21:1): He said "lil-nas" (for the people), although the reckoning is for them and against them. Does "lil-nas" mean "for their benefit"? That does not appear to be so, because He said after it: ﴿while they are heedless, turning away﴾ (21:1).

So the reckoning is not in their benefit; rather, the reckoning is against them. Then how could it be in such a context ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near﴾ (21:1), when the matter is against the disbelievers? It should have said: "iqtaraba 'ala al-nas hisabuhum" (drawn near upon the people).

We say: That would be the case if the lam were taken as belonging to the reckoning. Rather, the lam here belongs to "iqtaraba" (drew near), not to the reckoning; that is, it drew near to the people, and the reckoning is for them or against them. That is a different matter.

As for His saying: ﴿while they are heedless, turning away﴾ (21:1): "al-ghafla" (heedlessness) means moving a thing away from the mind where it should be kept, so that it is not moved from it. It was obligatory that they remember it and not be heedless of it. Heedlessness ("ghafla") is not the same as forgetfulness ("nisyan"), because heedlessness is to neglect a matter that must not be neglected and must not be absent from your mind, whereas forgetfulness is beyond your will.

Their heedlessness here is about the root and summit of religion, which is belief in divinity. If one believes in divinity, then heedlessness concerns the rulings that religion brought, and these are the sins. The discussion here concerns the disbelievers, as evidenced by His saying after it: ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed﴾ (21:2). Heedlessness of the Supreme Lord is like heedlessness of the Supreme Lord's command, and there is a difference between one heedlessness and another.

The Prophet (ﷺ) told his companions about this heedlessness, as Sayyiduna Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman narrated, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related to us two hadiths: I have seen one of them, and I am awaiting the other. He told us: ("Trust was sent down into the root of men's hearts"). "Trust" (al-amanah) is true faith in Allah, that is, faith settled and established in the heart, and we uttered the testimony. ("Then the Qur'an was revealed, and they learned from the Qur'an and learned from the Sunnah.") Then he told us about the removal of trust, saying: ("A man sleeps a sleep, and trust is taken from his heart"), that is, he becomes heedless with a heedlessness, ("and its trace remains like the trace of a wakt"). The wakt is like a cigarette, for example, that falls on the skin and burns it, so that its colour changes. ("Then he sleeps a sleep"), that is, another time, ("and trust is taken from his heart, and its trace remains like the trace of a majl"). The majl is a coal of fire, ("so it blisters, and you see it raised and swollen, though there is nothing in it"), that is, swollen. ("So people then ..." meaning after the removal of trust) "trade with one another, and hardly anyone among them fulfils trust, until it is said: 'In the tribe of so-and-so there is a trustworthy man,'" because trustworthiness is rare among people.

Then the narrator says: ("A time has passed over me when I did not care which of you I traded with: if he was a Muslim, his religion would return it to me; and if he was a Jew or a Christian, his ruler would return it to me." Meaning: if he cheated me in something or some error occurred in the sale), ("and if he was a Jew or a Christian, his ruler would return it to me"), that is, the people charged with overseeing the markets, who are the officials of hisbah (market oversight), so if they saw cheating they prevented it and returned to the owner of the right his right. ("But now I hardly trade with any of you except so-and-so and so-and-so.")(5) If this was in their days, what of our days?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke truly when he said: ("People are like a hundred camels; you hardly find among them a riding beast.")(6) That is, despite their number, you do not find among them a camel that will carry your saddle and carry you.

In another narration: ("Trials are presented to hearts like a mat, strand by strand"), that is, like the weaving of a mat, strand after strand, until the mat is completed. Then ("a stain" falls on the heart).(7)

So the heedlessness of these people is heedlessness of the summit and of divinity, not of the obligations, because they are not believers in the Obligator, glorified is He.

As for His saying: ﴿turning away﴾ (21:1): does it indicate deliberate contrivance, that they are deliberately contriving this turning away?

(1) Ahmad in his Musnad (6/441) and Abdullah ibn Ahmad in his Zawa'id on his father's Musnad, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ("Allah created Adam when He created him, and struck his right shoulder, and brought forth a white offspring as if they were ants; and He struck his left shoulder, and brought forth a black offspring as if they were coals. He said to those in His right hand: 'To Paradise, and I do not mind.' And He said to those in His left hand: 'To the Fire, and I do not mind.'")
(2) Al-judhr: the origin of everything. In the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: "The trust was sent down into the judhr of men's hearts," that is, into its root. (Lisan al-Arab, entry: j-dh-r)
(3) Al-wakt: a slight trace in a thing, like a dot differing from its colour. (Lisan, entry: w-k-t)
(4) Al-nafta: a blister that appears on the hand from work, filled with water. Abu Zayd said: when there is water between the skin and the flesh. (Lisan, entry: n-f-t)
(5) Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7086) and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (143), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him.
(6) A hadith agreed upon. Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6498), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2547), from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (11/335): (The meaning: you do not find among a hundred camels one fit for riding, for what is fit for riding should be gentle and easy to lead; likewise you do not find among a hundred people one fit for companionship, who helps his companion and is gentle toward him.)
(7) Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/386, 405), and Muslim in his Sahih (144), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and its completion: ("Whatever heart absorbs them, a black spot is made in it, and whatever heart rejects them, a white spot is made in it.")
(8) Al-ran and al-rayn: it is whatever overcomes and covers you. Al-rayn: the blackness of the heart from sins. The root of rayn: sealing and covering. (Lisan al-Arab, entry: r-y-n)

Then the Almighty, glorified is He, says: ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed, except that they listen to it while they play.﴾

That is: a reminder from the Qur'an, ﴿newly revealed﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:2), meaning: they hear it as something new, for the first time. ﴿Except that they listen to it while they play﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:2): they give it no attention and pay it no heed, and they do this deliberately, urging one another to it and inciting against it, as the Almighty says, relating their words: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it, that you may overcome."﴾ (Fussilat 41:26).

They fear that if they hear the Qur'an they will be affected by it and believe. Therefore, "do not listen to it; rather, create noise around it so that no one hears it in quiet and tranquility and believes in it." This means that this act is in their interest, because they cannot refute the arguments of the Qur'an, nor stand firm before its inimitability, its eloquence, or its effect upon souls. So they have no option but to divert people from hearing it and to disrupt it, so that it cannot reach the ears, penetrate the hearts, and mix with them as faith.

Al-la'b (play, la'ib): is that you occupy yourself with an action that has no purpose or aim, as a small child takes his brother's notebook and scribbles in it with a pen without order and without goal.

There is also al-lahw (diversion, lahw): an action that is purposeful and has an aim, but this aim is set by you for yourself, or set by another who wants to corrupt you through it. So it is a purposeful action with an aim, not merely scribbling (shakhbata), like someone who busies himself, for example, with drawing pictures for amusement, or with solving crosswords, for these are actions with no benefit.

As for the beneficial work that a person should occupy himself with, it is that which is laid down for you by one higher than you, who is wise and loves you. These qualities are found only in God. Therefore, everything that distracts you from what your God has laid down for you is lahw, because it has diverted you from what is more important.

Hence the Exalted says: ﴿The life of this world is only play and diversion.﴾ (Muhammad 47:36).

Play belongs to the stage of childhood. Indeed, we bring play to the child and say to him: "Play." But diversion is that you occupy yourself with a purposeful action that has an aim, yet it distracts you from a loftier aim, which the Wise, the Capable, the Highest above you, who loves you, has set for you.

So the extreme of diversion and play is that they play upon hearing the Qur'an, and so they do not listen to it, not even as diversion with an aim; rather it is play with no aim and no benefit, because its aim is harmful.

Play, though permissible in the period before puberty, nevertheless hearts must be trained to turn toward God, the Mighty and Majestic, the Creator and Provider, during this early stage of human life. This is the duty of the father: if he brings his son food or drink, he says in front of the small child: "Our Lord has provided us with it." Likewise, in all matters of life he attributes the affair to God and reminds the small child: "Say: In the name of God. Say: Praise be to God."

In this way you train in the child his inner sense upon strong certainty in God. Even if the child does not see Him, he sees His signs and His blessings, and he sees his father who looks after him and brings him everything, and does not seek glory for himself but attributes everything to God.

So his father, who is his ideal, removes these matters from himself and ascribes them to God, and thus the child's inner sense is trained in faith. If the child is not raised with this upbringing, play and diversion creep into his soul.

We have said before that every action must arise from some inner motive among the motives of the heart, and no action arises without a motive except the action of a madman. The hearts are what direct the limbs, and if the hearts were not heedless, the limbs would not play.

Therefore, our master 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when he entered upon a man who was toying with his beard while praying, as many do, said: "If this man's heart were humble, his limbs would be humble."(1) The movement of the limbs is thus evidence of the heart's preoccupation. That is why the Almighty says after it: ﴿Their hearts are heedless, and the wrongdoers conspire in secret: "Is this not but a human like you? Will you then approach magic while you see?"﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:3).

1 Al-Imam al-Ghazali cited it in Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din (1/151) from a hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Al-'Iraqi said in his takhrij of the Ihya': (al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim reported it in al-Nawadir from a hadith of Abu Hurayra with a weak chain, because it is a saying of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib; Ibn Abi Shayba narrated it in al-Musannaf, and in it is a man who is not named).

And would that each of them did this deed within himself. Rather, they conspire together against the truth to corrupt it through play and diversion. ﴿And they secretly conferred...﴾ (21:3). That is: they hold private consultations in sin and keep them hidden, meaning they make them secret. The *najwa* (private consultation, secret conferring) or *tanaajī* is the lowering of the voice, as in God's words: ﴿There is no private conference of three but that He is the fourth of them, nor of five but that He is the sixth of them...﴾ (58:7).

So do not think that you are concealed from God, or that you hide anything from Him.

You will notice, in the progression of numbers in this verse, that it does not mention two. It begins with three, because private conferring is usually not between two but between three, where two confer so that the third does not hear.

Nor does it mention the numbers in order. It does not say, for example, "nor four but that He is the fifth of them," because the verse does not intend a numerical sequence. It merely gives you examples and samples of numbers.

Likewise in His words: ﴿Have you not considered those who were forbidden from private conferring, then they return to what they were forbidden and confer with one another in sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger...﴾ (58:8).

Since they hide words and keep them secret, they must be contrary to the sound *fitra* (innate human disposition). Had it been true, they would have said it openly. Thus the private conferring is evidence of their guilt in intellect, in heart, and in everything.

As for His words concerning the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O you who believe, when you consult the Messenger privately, offer a charity before your private consultation...﴾ (58:12).

Did the Companions speak to the Messenger in secret? No, but here there is another indication, which His words clarify: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among you like the call of some of you to others...﴾ (24:63).

The meaning is that we should not raise our voices in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) as happens among us when one speaks to another. Rather, we should speak to him as one speaks to someone to be revered, and maintain with him courtesy and humility.

As for His words: ﴿And they secretly conferred, those who did wrong...﴾ (21:3): is the word *alladhina* ("those who") here the subject of *asarru* ("they secretly conferred")? The grammatical rule is: if the verb precedes the subject, it takes the singular form. We say *akala al-qawm* ("the people ate"), not *akalu al-qawm*. Here, ﴿And they secretly conferred...﴾ (21:3): if *alladhina zalamu* ("those who did wrong") were the subject, it would say *wa-asarra alladhi zalamu*. Rather, the subject is the pronoun of the plural (the *waw* of plurality), followed by the relative pronoun *alladhina* after it. So it is not the subject, and this is not one of the correct usages of the Arabic language.

It is as if a questioner asked: "And who secretly conferred?" and the answer was: *alladhina zalamu* ("those who did wrong"). The word *zalamu* is general in wrongdoing. They first wronged themselves, because their wrong returns upon them as punishment. And wronging oneself arises from wronging the Supreme Truth: ﴿Indeed, associating others with God is a tremendous wrong﴾ (31:13).

Then they wronged people in other matters and in their rights. But *zalamu* came general, because a single wrong encompasses all kinds of wrong. Since it has reached the point that they wronged God, it is no wonder that they wrong what is beneath Him.

So what is the private conferring that the people kept secret, and who informed the Messenger of God of it?

The private conferring is His words: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does God not punish us for what we say?"﴾ (58:8).

How did Muhammad know this saying, when they said it within themselves and kept it secret? Should these people not have paid attention: how did Muhammad know their saying? The One who informed him of what was happening is his Lord, the Supreme God, from whom nothing is hidden. They should have turned their attention to the Lord of Muhammad, God, the true God who knows the hidden of everything, so that they would refrain from what they were doing. Instead of occupying their minds with matters of polytheism, they should have arrived through them at faith.

Among what came in their private conferring: ﴿Is this not but a human being like you?﴾ (21:3). So they denied that he could be a messenger because he was a human being, and a messenger must be an angel.

﴿Will you then approach magic while you see?﴾ (21:3). So they called the Qur'an magic, because they saw magic separate the son from his father and the brother from his brother. ﴿While you see﴾ (21:3): that the Qur'an does the like of this.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 4:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) says, subhanahu: ﴿He said: "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ (4)

It is as if a questioner asks: "From where do you have all this, O Muhammad, when the people have kept it secret?" ﴿He said: "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth..."﴾ (4) (al-Anbiya', 21:4): nothing hidden is concealed from Him. ﴿"And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ (4) (al-Anbiya', 21:4): All-Hearing of what is said and what is whispered, All-Knowing of what is done. Thus the events (al-ahdath) are sayings and deeds.

Among what they also said: ﴿"Rather, they say: 'A confusion of dreams!' Rather, he has invented it. Rather, he is a poet. Let him bring us a sign, as the earlier messengers were sent."﴾ (5)

(1) Adghath ahlam (confused dreams): that is, dreams that are varied, mixed, jumbled and indistinct, not distinguished, by way of metaphor, like mixed-up things. (al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/394).

(Bal) means that they persisted and did not stop at what they had said; rather, they also said ﴿Confused dreams...﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 21:5). And adghath (confused, jumbled) is the plural of dghth (ḍigh), which is a bundle of grass of mixed shapes, as came in the story of Ayyub, peace be upon him: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth) and strike with it and do not break your oath﴾ (Sad 38:44). That is: a bundle of grass stalks.

It also occurs in the dream of the Ruler of Egypt: ﴿They said, "Confused dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."﴾ (Yusuf 12:44).

As for His saying ﴿Rather, he has invented it...﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 21:5): that is, they persisted and said: he deliberately fabricated it and forged it. ﴿Rather, he is a poet...﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 21:5). So then: their statements and accusations against the Messenger of Allah are contradictory as to what he actually is. This is evidence of their confusion. Sometimes they deny that he is human, sometimes they say he is a sorcerer, sometimes they say he is a fabricator, and now they say he is a poet!!

We had already refuted all these accusations and said that they carry within them the proof of their lying and their fabrication against the Messenger of Allah.

Then they say ﴿So let him bring us a sign as the earlier ones were sent [with signs]﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 21:5). It is as if the sign of the Qur'an did not convince them, so they are not satisfied with it, and they demand another sign like those brought by the predecessors. The Qur'an responds to them on this matter: even if they would believe were the sign they proposed to come to them, We would have sent it down to them. Rather, past precedents confirm that they will not believe no matter what signs come to them, and this is one of the causes of punishment.

Al-Sha'rawi has made clear that Allah, glory be to Him, will not punish them as long as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among them. Therefore He did not grant them what they asked for of signs, because Allah, exalted is He, does not break His promise. If the sign came to them and they did not believe in it, the punishment would certainly descend upon them. For this reason, He, exalted is He, says after this: ﴿Not believed before them any town which We destroyed. Will they then believe?﴾

So: this experience has passed with others among the earlier nations, and they, like those before them, if We had sent down the sign to them, would not have believed, just as their predecessors did not believe: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ (al-An'am)

Then the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾

The Almighty responds to their objection to the humanity of the Messenger and their demand that the Messenger be an angel, as they said elsewhere: ﴿Shall mere mortals guide us?﴾ (al-Taghabun).

That is: they are like us, and they are not better than us, so how could they guide us? Does the Messenger guide you by his humanity, or by something that came to him from above? Is his method from himself?

The Messenger is not a social reformer; rather, he is one who conveys from God, your Lord and our Lord. Precedent has already been established among those before you that the Messenger should be a man: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed...﴾ (al-Anbiya). That is: had We sent an angel to them, the Messenger would have come to you as an angel. ﴿So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know﴾ (al-Anbiya): they are the Jews and the Christians. Did We send to them men or angels?

This is because it is required of a prophet that he be an example and a model for his people: a conveyer of a method, and a pattern of conduct. He realizes the method from God and then applies it to himself. He does not impose on people a matter from which he himself stands aloof(1); rather, he is their model and exemplar. A basic condition of exemplarity is that the genus be unified between the one who follows and the one who is followed.

Suppose you saw in the forest a lion charging, roaming and preying. Would you ever think of becoming a lion? Would you take the lion as your model? No, because your model must be of your own kind. But if you see a horseman on his steed charging and striking the enemies right and left, there is no doubt you would wish to be like him.

Likewise, if the Prophet had come as an angel, and the angels do not disobey God in what He commands them and they do what they are commanded, [then]—we are human beings, and even if the Messenger had come to us as an angel, he would have come to us in human form.

The Almighty says: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has God sent a mortal as a messenger?" Say: "If there had been in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ (al-Isra').

The Almighty responds to them: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they confuse [themselves].﴾ (al-An'am). Thus the doubt remains in place.

Therefore: it is not possible for the Messenger to the humans to be other than from among the humans. Yes, Muhammad is a human, but a human to whom revelation is made, as the noble hadith states: (It comes to me—that is, from the Highest Truth—and I say: I am not like any of you; and it is taken from me, and I say: I am only a human like you).

As for His saying ﴿So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know﴾ (al-Anbiya): that is, if you are in doubt about this statement, ask the people of the reminder among the earlier ones: the Jews and the Christians, the People of the Book(2).

And He said ﴿if you do not know﴾ (al-Anbiya): because it is a matter whose knowledge is doubtful.

1 Al-najwa: what is raised up from the earth. Abu Zayd said: the najwa is the elevated place which you think will save you. (Lisan al-Arab – root: n-j-w).
2 Sufyan said it, and Ibn Zayd said: by "the reminder" He meant the Qur'an, i.e., ask the believing scholars among the people of the Qur'an. Jabir al-Ju'fi said: when this verse was revealed, he (may God be pleased with him) said: we are the people of the reminder. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4447).

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾

﴿Ja'alnāhum (We made them).. (8)﴾ (al-Anbiya’): That is: the Messengers. ﴿jasadan (bodies).. (8)﴾ (al-Anbiya’): meaning: a thing cast and solid, which is not eaten, not drunk, and does not move. Rather, they are human beings who eat and drink like any human, walk in the markets, and live the ordinary life of human beings. ﴿wa-mā kānū khālidīn (nor were they immortal) (8)﴾ (al-Anbiya’): Immortality is not a attribute of human beings, and [the Messengers' followers] followed the Messengers and knew this truth about them. And Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die.﴾ (30) (az-Zumar).

Then the Truthful, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, so We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾

This is one of the established practices (sunan) of God regarding the messengers: that He fulfills His promise to them. Have you ever seen a messenger whose people opposed him, fought him and persecuted him, and whose end was that they triumphed over him?

Did not the Truthful, blessed and exalted, say: ﴿And已 Our word had already preceded to Our servants the messengers. Indeed they would be the ones given victory. And indeed Our hosts, they would be the victorious.﴾ (al-Saffat).

The fulfilling of the promise was that We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors. The transgressors (al-musrifun) are those who exceed the known limit. Thus the ultimate end of all the messengers is victory from God, and His fulfilment of what He promised them.

Al-Haqq (exalted be He) addresses those who denied the Prophet: "We did not send down to you any sign remote from your knowledge. Rather, We sent to you a Messenger with a sign of the same kind as that in which you excel (nabagtum fihi), and when it was revealed you understood it and recognised its aims." The proof of this is that the Qur'an contains expressions that strike one as strange, yet you did not object to them, nor did you accuse Muhammad of error in them, although you were searching for a mistake in him and seeking a slip on his part.

For example, when (Alif-Lam-Mim) was revealed, we did not hear any of them say: "O believers in Muhammad, Muhammad claims that he has brought an inimitable book; ask him: what is the meaning of (Alif-Lam-Mim)?" This indicates that they understood it and accepted it, and found in it no opening against the Messenger of Allah, because the Arabs, in their language and their manner of speech, use these letters as an alert (tanbih).

Speech is an embassy between the speaker and the listener. The speaker is not taken by surprise by his own words; rather, he prepares them and brings them to mind before he utters them. The listener, however, may be surprised by the speaker's words, and may be heedless, needing someone to wake him and alert him so that nothing escapes him.

Thus, tools of alerting have been established in the language: if you wish to speak about something important, of which you fear some part may be missed, you alert the listener. Among this is the saying of 'Amr ibn Kulthum(1):

* Alā hubbī bi-ṣaḥnika fa-aṣbiḥīnā(2) *

and another's saying:

Alā an'im ṣabāḥan ayyuhā al-ṭalal al-bālī(3)

wa-hal yan'amanna man kāna fī al-'aṣr al-khālī(4)

Therefore: (alā) here is merely a particle of alerting; that is, "Listen and pay attention to what I say."

Likewise is the style of the Qur'an: ﴿Surely the friends of Allah—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾ (Yunus 10:62), and ﴿Surely they fold their breasts…﴾ (Hud 11:5).

Therefore: when the Qur'an was revealed to them, they understood these letters, and perhaps they understood from them more than this, and they did not respond to the Messenger of Allah with any of these matters, despite their keen desire to criticise him and to take him to task.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿In it is your remembrance…﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:10): al-dhikr (remembrance): we have previously explained that dhikr is used to mean the Qur'an, or the revealed books, or fame and honour, or admonition, or glorification and praise of Allah.

Here dhikr may be intended to mean reminding them of God as Creator, and of His true method as a constitution. Had you paid heed to what the Qur'an brought, you would have known that innate nature (fitrah) guides to it and agrees with it, and you would have known that the Qur'an was not biased against you, as evidenced by the fact that it affirmed some matters you had been guided to by sound innate nature and agreed with you upon.

Among this, for example: the blood-money for homicide is the very same blood-money that the Qur'an prescribed; matters of betrothal, marriage and dower were existing practices which the Qur'an confirmed; many of them used to forbid wine and did not drink it, by innate nature; and many did not prostrate to idols. Therefore: sound innate nature may be guided to the truth and does not conflict with the method of God.

Or: the meaning of ﴿your remembrance…﴾ (21:10) may be: your nobility, your renown, your standing and your prominence among the nations. For the Qur'an, which was revealed for the whole world, was revealed in your language. It is as if God Almighty turns the minds of all people to your language and turns their hearts towards it, and urges them to learn it, to know it, to speak it and to spread it among people; whoever cannot do so translates it. And what nobility is greater than this?

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ (21:10): i.e., will you not employ your minds and reflect that your good lies in this Qur'an? If you seek character and religion, it is in the Qur'an; if you seek nobility, reputation and renown, it is in the Qur'an. And what nobility is greater than people saying: "The Prophet is Arab, and the Qur'an is Arabic"?

1 He is 'Amr ibn Kulthum ibn Malik, of the Banu Taghlib, Abu al-Aswad, a pre-Islamic poet of the first rank. Born in northern Arabia in the lands of Rabi'ah, he was among the most dignified of men; he became leader of his people Taghlib while still a youth, and lived to an old age. He died in the Euphrates region of the Jazira in the year 40 BH. (al-A'lam by al-Zirikli 5/84).
2 The first half of the opening line of the Mu'allaqa of 'Amr ibn Kulthum. Al-ṣaḥn: a great bowl; plural: ṣuḥūn. The meaning of the line: "Awake from your sleep, O cupbearer, and give me the morning draught in your great bowl, and do not withhold the wine of this village." (See Sharh al-Mu'allaqat al-Sab' by al-Zuzuni, p. 165).
3 Al-ṭalal: what remains visible of the traces of dwellings. (Lisan al-Arab, root ṭ-l-l).
4 The line is by Imru' al-Qays, cited by al-Zuzuni in Sharh al-Mu'allaqat al-Sab', p. 102 (footnote).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And how many a town did We shatter, which had been wrongdoing, and We brought into being after it another people.﴾

Qasamna (we shattered): al-qasm is a breaking that cannot be mended. It is as if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, places before their eyes the cities that denied and did wrong, so that they may take from them a lesson and an admonition. It is therefore no marvel that We should break the backs of the deniers; rather, there are many precedents for this in history.(1)

Therefore He said: ﴿And how many a town did We shatter...﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:11). Here kam (how many) is khabariyyah (informative), indicating a multitude that cannot be counted. So beware: if you turn your necks away, there may befall you what befell them.

And His saying: ﴿And We brought into being after it another people﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:11) means: there succeeded them other successors.

(1) Al-Qurtubi said here in his tafsir (6/4449): "He means cities that were in Yemen. The people of tafsir and of reports said: he meant the people of Hadur (Hadhur), and to them had been sent a prophet named Shu'ayb ibn Dhi Mahdam, and he is not Shu'ayb the companion of Madyan."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 12:

"When they perceived Our punishment" – ﴿هُم مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 21:12): that is, so that the punishment would not overtake them. Rakd (running) is swift running at a trot, and its original sense is the rakḍ of the mount, meaning striking it with the leg so that it hastens. Among its uses is ﴿اركض برجلك﴾ (Sad 38:42), meaning: strike the ground with your foot so that water comes out, ﴿هذا مغتسل بارد وشراب﴾ (Sad 38:42), "This is a cool bath and a drink."

In this verse there is one of the features of Qur'anic inimitability (i'jaz). Ayyub (peace be upon him) was afflicted with a disease in his skin, and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, willed for him to be healed. He was told: strike the earth with your foot, and there will come forth for you cool water, from which there is a bath and from which there is a drink. So the water here is a remedy that treats two matters: it treats the outward and the inward.

The pitfall of healers is that when they see, for example, blisters and boils on the skin, they treat them with ointments by which the wound heals, but these do not treat the causes of the phenomenon from within. As for the divine treatment, the bath is a cure for the phenomenon, and the drink is a cure for the causes of the phenomenon within the body.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 13:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Do not flee, but return to what you were made to enjoy of luxury and your dwellings, that you may be questioned.﴾

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, in the story of these deniers, presented the outcome of the punishment, saying: ﴿How many a town have We shattered...﴾ (21:11). Then He detailed the shattering: when they sensed the punishment, they left their town and hastened away fleeing, lest the punishment overtake them. Here He says to them: Do not flee, and return to your dwellings and to what you were made to enjoy of luxury.

Al-taraf (luxury) is ease and indulgence. We say: taraf al-rajul yatrafu, like faraha yafrahu, meaning he indulged in comfort. When a hamza is added to it, and it is said atraf al-rajul, its meaning is: he took comfort and was made insolent by it.

Among its uses also: atrafahu Allah, meaning: God deceived them with comfort, so that it would be a punishment for them.

So His saying here, ﴿to what you were made to enjoy of luxury﴾ (21:13), from atrafahu Allah, means: He gave them comfort whose due they did not fulfil, so that punishment would be drawn upon them. But since God, exalted is He, intends punishment for them, why does He grant them comfort?

They said: There is a difference between one punishment and two punishments. Punishment is that you inflict on a person something that pains him. But if you pamper him and elevate him and then punish him, you have inflicted on him punishment upon punishment.

We have illustrated this by saying: if you want to bring down your enemy, you do not drop him from a mat, for example; rather you lift him up so that it is more severe for him and more painful.

From this is the Qur'an's saying: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of every thing...﴾ (6:44): We gave them health, wealth, rank, land, houses and palaces. ﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair﴾ (6:44). Thus is His seizing painful and severe; in proportion to how high God raised them, so will be their punishment.

Another point in His saying, ﴿We opened for them...﴾ (6:44), is that it is not for their benefit, as in: ﴿Indeed We have opened for you a clear victory﴾ (48:1). So all of this is not in their interest; rather it is a calamity upon them. Do not be deceived by it: God has given it to them, and they will become insolent with it, so it will be the cause of their punishment.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that you may be questioned﴾ (21:13): that is, return to your dwellings, your palaces, and the luxury you were in, perhaps someone will pass by you and ask you: where is the luxury you were in? Where has it gone? But what they are now in of disgrace will silence their tongues, and they will say nothing of what happened; rather their words and conduct will be: ﴿They said: Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers﴾ (21:14).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 14:

When the deniers sensed the might of God and His punishment, they tried to flee so as to escape the punishment. Then (it was said) to them: "Return to what you were in, for no thing will save you from the punishment of God, and no fugitive can escape the punishment of God." When they found themselves in this position, they found nothing but regret, so they turned to their own selves to reproach them and to pass judgment upon them that they deserved what had befallen them.

As for their saying, ﴿Woe to us!﴾ (21:14): they are calling out to the punishment, just as you say, "Woe is me!" (ya bu'sī) or "Woe to my misery!" (ya shaqā'ī). And does anyone call out to punishment, misery, or wretchedness? A person only calls out for what delights him.

The meaning is: "O my woe, come, for this is your time." For nothing will heal him from the past except that he regret it and feel remorse for what he did. So now they feel regret, now they know that they deserve the punishment, and they blame themselves.

﴿Indeed, we were wrongdoers﴾ (21:14): wrongdoers toward ourselves, through our wronging of our Lord in that we disbelieved in Him, just as He said in another verse: ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected concerning God..."﴾ (39:56).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 15:

Allah's statement: ﴿So they continued to say that claim of theirs,﴾ (al-Anbiya', 15). That is, their saying: ﴿"Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers."﴾ (al-Anbiya', 14). They did not say it only once, as one might say it in a moment of emotion; rather it became their constant habit, and they took it up as a form of glorification: "Woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers! Woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers!" Nothing relieves their hearts except this word, which they keep repeating, just as a criminal sits consoling himself in regret, saying: "I was mistaken, I deserve prison, such and such."

And Allah's statement: ﴿until We made them as cut-down stubble, extinguished,﴾ (al-Anbiya', 15). Ḥaṣīd (cut-down stubble) means the mahsūd, that is, the crop after it has been harvested. ﴿Khāmidīn﴾ (extinguished) (al-Anbiya', 15): khumūd (extinguishing) is one of the attributes of fire after it was blazing, flaming and burning, and has become extinguished; then it turns to ash and its heat departs. It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is pointing to their heat in their hostility toward the Messenger, their disputation and their obstinacy with him (ﷺ), and this fire has been extinguished and has become ash.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾

Our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, gives us the highest example in creation, for the creation of the heavens and the earth is a great matter: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind...﴾ (Ghafir 40:57). Man is born, dies and is renewed, whereas the heaven and the earth and what lies between them of stars and planets is a tremendous, mighty creation, precisely ordered and systematically arranged throughout this long span of time, with no flaw or malfunction having befallen it.

The Truth, glorified is He, did not need to create the heavens and the earth and what is between them, because they are the most wondrous of things; rather, they were created for mankind and made subservient to serve them. The heaven and what is in it of sun, moon, stars, air, rain and clouds, and the earth and what is upon it of bounties, and even what is beneath it as well: ﴿and what is beneath the soil﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:6).

Everything is created for you, O human being. Even what you imagine as serving others ultimately pours out before you and in your hands: inanimate matter serves plants, plants serve animals, and all of them serve man.

So if man is the highest served being in this universe, what is his work, and what is his function in God's universe? Everything beneath you has a task it performs, so what is your task? Thus: if you have no purpose in life, you are more worthless than animals, than plants, even than inanimate matter. You must therefore seek for yourself a work that suits your lordship over these creatures.

Moreover, did these creatures subjugate themselves to you by themselves, or did God subjugate them and make them pliable for your service? It was incumbent upon you to pay attention to the One who subjected these creatures to you, though they are stronger than you. Have you power over the heaven? Can you reach the sun and the moon? ﴿Indeed you will not rend the earth, nor will you reach the mountains in height﴾ (al-Isra 17:37).

Thus, you should have sought with your intellect the One who subjected all this to you; you should have been guided to the Creator of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, for He, glorified is He, did not create them in vain, nor did He create them for play; rather, He created them for your sake.

Therefore, the Almighty says in the Hadith Qudsi: "O son of Adam, I created things for your sake, and I created you for My sake, so do not occupy yourself with what is yours at the expense of Him to whom you belong."

The universe is owned by you, and you are owned by God, so do not occupy yourself with what is owned by you at the expense of the Owner of you.

What, then, is the wisdom behind creating the heaven and the earth and what is between them? The wisdom is that, were it not for these creatures, we would not be able to infer the capable power behind the creation of these things, namely the Creator, glorified is He. Thus they are for demonstrating the attributes of majesty and beauty of God, Mighty and Majestic is He. If someone claimed to be a poet—and to God belongs the highest example—we would say to him: where is the poem you have composed? We know that he is a poet only through his poetry and the works he claims. Is this not a claim without proof?

God created this creation for your sake, and left you to dwell in it, and created it subjugated and driven: the sun has never objected one day to rising, and the moon, the stars, the rain, the air, the earth and the plants all give to the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient alike, because they operate by subjugation, not by will and choice. As for man, he is the created being possessing choice in whether he acts or does not act.

If you look at this universe, you can divide it into two parts: a part in which you have no involvement at all, which you see harmonious in its order, uprightness and precision; and a part in which you intervene, and this is where disorder and corruption occur.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And the sun runs on to a stationary place for it; that is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing. And for the moon We have measured stations until it returns like the old dried palm stalk(1). It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each is floating in an orbit.﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:38–40).

The universe around you moves by the command of its Creator, precisely ordered, nothing in it deviating. If you were to take, for example, a full year of 365 days and then try to repeat it in another year, you would find that the sun rose on the first day from the same place, and on the second day from the same place as the second day, and so on, with extreme precision. Glory be to its Creator!

Therefore, those who set calendars to know the times set up a calendar of thirty-three years, recording the cycle of the heavens, and then what they recorded recurs with very strict regularity. Likewise, for example, when scientists determine the time of an eclipse, whether it is partial or annular, when you follow it you find it exactly regular at its appointed time. This is evidence of the regularity and perfection of this universe, because we have no intervention in it at all.

On the other hand, look at anything in which man intervenes: for example, some of us measure out for others, weigh for others, measure for others, bake for others, sell to others... etc. Look at these relationships, and you will find them—except for those whom God has mercy upon—corrupt and disordered, unless they proceed upon the way of God; if they proceed upon the way of God they become upright like the uprightness of the heavens and the earth.

Therefore: whenever you see something corrupt or ugly, know that man has poked his nose into it.

It is as if the Creator, Mighty and Majestic is He, says to man: you are not even trustworthy over yourself. I created for you this entire universe, and nothing in it has deviated, nor has any phenomenon gone awry; but you, because you are free to choose, have wronged yourself and worn yourself out.

Know that matters are secure with Me. If I take you from the world of causes to the Hereafter and to the Causer, I will be trustworthy over you, bestowing upon you a bliss with no toil, no fatigue, and no misery; and if you serve yourself in this world, I will serve you in the Hereafter, and fulfil your desire without you stirring a finger.

Therefore: if I occupied myself with the One who owns me, namely God, the Exalted, what I own would be set right for me.

So this universe and this existence God created to serve man. Why? As if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, were saying: it suffices Me from My creatures that they bear witness, choosing freely, that there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Although the creatures have borne this testimony under compulsion, the greatness lies in the one who chooses, who has the power to bear witness or not.

Moreover, after I have bestowed upon you all these blessings, I have sent down to you a method: do this and do not do that. If you obey, I will reward you, and if you disobey, I will punish you; and this is the purpose of creating the heaven and the earth, and that they were not created in play.

You know this method from the Messengers, and the Messengers know it from the Book. So if you deny the Messengers, you will not know these rulings or this method, and consequently we could not reward or punish you, and the creation of the heaven and the earth would be without purpose.

1 Al-'Arjun: it is the base of the palm frond's stalk, from which the clusters of dates branch out. Its first appearance is green, then it whitens, then yellows when the dates ripen; when it is cut and dries it becomes white. The moon at the end of the month is likened to it, because it is curved like a part of an arc, white and of little light. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/14).

Then the Almighty says: ﴿Had We wished to take up a pastime, We would have taken it from Our own presence, if We were to do so.﴾

So if He willed amusement, He would have done it, for He is capable of all things. His words ﴿if We were heedless..﴾ (21:17) indicate that this will never happen.

The meaning of *lahw* (diversion, idle play) is that one turns to an activity that has no aim and no benefit. The person who indulges in *lahw* leaves what is important and turns to what is unimportant. *Lahw* and *la'b* (play) are two movements of the limbs, but they are movements whose only purpose is the movement itself. They have no perfecting goal that one strives for through the movement. For this reason, *lahw* and *la'b* without a purpose are called *'abath* (aimless), and this is impossible with respect to God, glorified and exalted be He.

1. *Lahw*: a woman, in the language of Yemen, said Qatadah. ʿUqbah ibn Abi Jasrah said, and Tawus, ʿAta' and Mujahid came asking him about His words, ﴿Had We wished to take up a pastime..............(17)﴾ (21:17). He said: *lahw* is the wife. Al-Hasan also said it. Ibn ʿAbbas said: *lahw* is the child. Al-Hasan also said this. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4452).

Since they have engaged in idle play and have been ungrateful for the blessings of God in the heavens and the earth, let them know that this state will not last. God, glorified is He, gives respite to falsehood and enlarges it until it advances and spreads, and then, when He seizes it, He seizes it as the Mighty, the Omnipotent, and He hurls the truth against it.

As for His saying: ﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes away.﴾ [21:18] "Qadhf" (hurling) means throwing with force, like destructive projectiles. ﴿Fa-yadmaghuhu﴾ (and it crushes it): it is said "damaghahu," meaning he struck his brain (dimagh). The brain is the noblest of the human organs, for it contains the medulla (al-mukh), which is the measure of a person. If the medulla is sound, any other malfunction can be repaired; but if the medulla is disabled, there is no hope of survival after it.

For this reason, God, glorified and exalted is He, made the bone of the skull the strongest bone of the body, to protect this vital organ. Doctors, for example, do not pronounce a person dead when the heart stops, because the heart can be restored to its work by a particular kind of massage, and so can breathing. But if the medulla stops, its owner has died. It is the first cell, and it retains the last manifestations of life in the body; hence they say "clinical death."

The essence of nutrition reaches the medulla, which is the highest served organ among the organs. The body takes from food what suffices its energy for work, and what exceeds its energy is stored as fat, on which the body feeds when food is absent. When the fat is exhausted, it feeds on muscle, then on bone, in order to supply the medulla with what it needs. It is the master of the body, and after it the other organs are nourished.

Thus, everything in the body serves the medulla, because it is the highest of the organs. As for plants, for example, they serve their lowest part: when water dries up in the soil and the plant does not find sufficient nourishment, it feeds on its top, so it wilts first, then its leaves fall, then the small branches dry up, then the trunk, then the root.

Of this is the saying of our master Zakariyya, peace be upon him: ﴿He said, "My Lord, my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with grey hair"﴾ [19:4]. The bone is the last storehouse of nourishment in the body, so the weakening of the bone is a sign that the matter has nearly reached its end.

Therefore, His saying ﴿fa-yadmaghuhu﴾ means that it strikes him in the most important of the organs, its master and the one that controls it, not in another organ that can be mended. For this reason He says after it: ﴿fa-idha huwa zahiq﴾ (and behold, it vanishes away). Zahiq means departing with violence.

As for His saying: ﴿And woe to you for what you describe﴾ [21:18], it means: O human being, deluded by your obstinacy and stubbornness in falsehood, who has set your mind and heart against confronting the truth — We shall hurl the truth against your falsehood, strike your brain, and it will vanish away. At that moment you will say, "Woe is me," as they said before: ﴿O woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers﴾ [21:14], when they came into direct contact with the punishment.

The meaning of ﴿tasifun﴾ (you describe): you lie with a fabricated lie. For instance, if you see a beautiful person and say, "His face describes beauty," meaning: if you want a description of beauty, look at his face, which gives you an image of beauty. As in His saying: ﴿and their tongues describe falsehood﴾ [16:62], meaning: if you want to know falsehood itself, listen to their speech and what their tongues have said.

As they say: "a tale of Kharafa"(1). The origin of this saying is a man named Kharafa who used to say: "I have an arrow which, if I shoot it at a gazelle, will pursue it; if it turns right, it pursues it; if it goes left, it pursues it; if it climbs the mountain, it climbs after it; if it descends, it descends after it." As if his arrow were a guided missile like the ones we see today!! So his speech became a proverb for falsehood(2).

Therefore the poet said:

*"A tale of Kharafa, O Umm 'Amr"*

If you want a definition of falsehood, I will not define it for you as a statement that does not conform to reality. Rather, listen to their speech: it is the most truthful description of falsehood, because it is an exposed and disgraced lie.

Among the same is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Glory be to God above what they describe﴾ [37:159; cited here as 6:100 in the source]: that is, they lie and fabricate against God.

Someone may say: Why does God give respite to falsehood, so that it rebels and rises, and then the truth overcomes it and crushes it?

We say: The wisdom in this is that trials may be fulfilled. People do not long for the truth except when they see the ugliness of falsehood, and they do not recognize the station of justice except when they see the ugliness of injustice. Things are distinguished by their opposites, as the poet said:

*"The face is like the dawn, white; and the hair is like the night, black.*
*Two opposites, when brought together in beauty, the opposite reveals the beauty of its opposite."*

So we do not know the beauty of truth except through the ugliness of falsehood, nor the sweetness of faith except through the bitterness of disbelief.

(1) Kharafa: an agreeable tale of falsehood. Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned that Kharafa, of the Banu Udhra or of Juhayna, was snatched away by jinn, then returned to his people and used to narrate tales of what he had seen that amazed people, so they called him a liar, and it passed into people's tongues. (Lisan al-'Arab, root kh-r-f.)

(2) Ahmad cited in his Musnad (6/157), from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, once told his wives a tale one night. One of them said: "O Messenger of God, it is as if the tale were a tale of Kharafa." He said: "Do you know what Kharafa is? Kharafa was a man of 'Udhra whom the jinn carried off in the Jahiliyya; he remained among them a long time, then they returned him to mankind, and he used to tell people what he had seen among them of marvels, so people said: 'a tale of Kharafa.'"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 19:

The Truthful (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, has already informed us that He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them. This is a container (ẓarf); so what is contained within it? What is contained within it is creation, and they too belong to Allah: ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth…﴾ (21:19). Although among creation there are those whom Allah has distinguished with choice, to believe or to disbelieve, to obey or to disobey, nevertheless, if one is free (mukhtar) in matters of obligation (taklif), he is subjugated (maqhur) in matters of cosmic existence (kawniyyah), in which he has no say.

So man has no control over his birth or his death, nor any control over his health and well-being, his sickness, his intelligence, his height or his shortness. Therefore, he is Allah's possession, subjugated to Him, except that He, glory be to Him, has left him a single domain of obligatory choice.

As for the heavens and the earth, they are subjected and subjugated: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it…﴾ (33:72).

So they chose subjection over the choice for which they had no capacity.

As for man, his intellect urged him to bear it, and he preferred choice, and he saw that he would direct this trust in the right direction: ﴿But man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant﴾ (33:72).

So his Lord described him as being, in this act, "unjust and ignorant," because he does not know the outcome of this bearing. If you say: what is the merit of the obedience of the heavens and the earth, when they are compelled? We say: they are compelled by their own choice, for Allah gave them the choice and they chose compulsion.

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are with Him do not disdain His worship…﴾ (21:19), meaning: they are not like you, who lie and disbelieve; rather, they are in constant worship that never ceases, and what is meant here is the angels, because they ﴿do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ (66:6).

﴿And they do not tire﴾ (21:19): from ḥasira, meaning he became weak, exhausted, fatigued, and was overtaken by boredom and exhaustion.

From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then return the gaze twice; your gaze will return to you humbled and weary﴾ (67:4): i.e., dull and weak, unable to face intense light, as when you face the sun's light or the direct light of a car, which prevents you from seeing; for the essential function of light is that we see by it what we cannot otherwise see.

In another verse He, exalted is He, says: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are near [to Him]﴾ (4:172), because their honour lies in this matter.

Therefore these angels worship God and glorify Him. Weakness does not befall them, nor lethargy, and they do not feel boredom from worship and from declaring Him far above all imperfection, glory be to Him. The angels do not show arrogance toward His worship and submission to Him.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate.﴾ (Al-A'raf: 206).

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who can raise the dead?﴾

That is: so what has come over them that they turn away from all these realities? Do they have gods besides Me, when I am the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and they, with all who are in them of humankind, jinn and angels, belong to Me? Everything is a servant of Mine, glorifying Me with My praise. So what has impressed them about other than Me, that they turn away from Me and head toward it? Is it better than Me, or closer to them than I am?

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is expressing astonishment at their turning away from the true God, to whom belongs all this dominion and all these favours and bounties.

As for His saying, ﴿they can raise the dead﴾ (al-Anbiya') : that is, they have the power to bring the dead to life and resurrect them. None of this has happened, because: ﴿Had there been in them gods besides Allah, both would have been ruined. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 21, verse 22:

Thus, with your turning away from the true God, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to whom all created things glorify Him, there is no other god. ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been corrupted.﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:22) That is: the discourse is still connected to the heavens and the earth. ﴿They would both have been corrupted.﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:22): the heavens and the earth, which are the containers of everything in the creation of Allah.

As for the meaning of ﴿except Allah﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:22): "illa" (except) is a particle of exception that removes what follows it from the ruling of what precedes it, as when you say: "The people came except Muhammad," for you have removed Muhammad from the ruling applying to the people, which is coming. If we take the verse according to this meaning, ﴿Had there been in them gods, Allah excepted, they would both have been corrupted﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:22), that is: if there were gods, with Allah outside of them, the heavens and the earth would be corrupted.

So what if we say: "Had there been gods, with Allah among them"? That would mean they would not be corrupted; so "illa", if it establishes the existence of Allah, does not prevent association with Allah, and this is not the intent of the verse, which affirms that there is no god other than Him.

Therefore, "illa" here is not a particle of exception. Rather, it is a noun meaning "ghayr" (other than), as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed."﴾ (Hud, 11:36)

The meaning, then: had there been in them gods described as other than Allah, they would both have been corrupted, so it is impossible that there be a partner.

There is another verse: ﴿Say: "If there were with Him other gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne."﴾ (Al-Isra', 17:42)

Allah the Exalted gives us the rational division in the Qur'an: let us suppose, for the sake of argument, that there are other gods. ﴿Say: "If there were with Him other gods, as they say, if...﴾ (Al-Isra', 17:42) That is: if this were to happen, ﴿they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne﴾ (Al-Isra', 17:42).

"Sabil" means the way; that is, they would have sought a path to the Lord of the Throne, meaning to Allah. Why? Either to contend with Him and confront Him, as to how He took divinity from behind their backs; or to draw near to Him and take divinity from within Him, and strength in the shade of His power, just as Allah the Exalted gave active power to fire, for example, from within His own power. Fire does not act of itself, but the true Agent is the One who created fire, as is shown by the fact that if He, glorified be He, willed, He would strip it of this power, as in the saying of the True One, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim."﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:69)

And His saying: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor has there been with Him any god; otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some would have overcome others.﴾ (Al-Mu'minun, 23:91) This noble verse and its like establish that He, glorified be He, exists and is One.

As for taking "illa" as an exception, it establishes that He exists, but that He has a partner and is not one. Therefore it is a noun meaning "ghayr," and since it is built like particles, its i'rab (grammatical case) appears on what follows it: "Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been corrupted." The i'rab of "ghayr" thus becomes the i'rab of "illa," which appears on the word Allah.

But why would the heavens and the earth be corrupted if there were gods in them other than Allah?

They said: because in this matter you face two possibilities: either these gods are equal in the attributes of perfection, or one has the attributes of perfection and the other has a deficiency. If they have the attributes of perfection, do they agree on creating things or disagree?

If they agree on creating something, this is pointless repetition, for one would create while the other has no work, and two influences do not combine on a single effect.

If they disagree about creation, one says: "This is mine," and the other says: "This is mine," and then some would overcome others.

As for when one has the attribute of perfection and the other has the attribute of deficiency, the one with deficiency cannot rightly be a god. Thus the True One, glorified and exalted be He, presents us with examples and clarifies them to make this truth manifest by reason and by transmission: there is no god but Allah, and taking gods with Him, glorified be He, is false.

Likewise, this answers those who call upon other gods besides Allah, such as those who said: Uzair is the son of Allah, those who said: the Messiah is the son of Allah, and those who took the angels as gods besides Allah: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord, which of them will be nearest.﴾ (Al-Isra', 17:57)

Those whom you call upon besides Allah seek a means of access to Him, draw near to Him, glorified be He, and look to see which of them is nearer to Allah than the other. How, then, could they be gods?

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:22) That is: exalted above what these people say. ﴿Above what they describe﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:22): that is, they distort, lie, and fabricate.

The "Arsh" (Throne) is the couch upon which a king sits, and it is the sign of kingship and dominion, as in the words of Allah the Exalted about the Queen of Sheba, in the speech of the hoopoe: ﴿I found a woman ruling over them, who has been given of everything, and she has a mighty throne.﴾ (Al-Naml, 27:23) So when He, glorified be He, says ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:22), it refers to His Throne, which nothing rises above and for which no other throne contends.

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq), glorified is He, says about Himself: ﴿He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ (21:23).

So Allah, exalted is He, is not questioned about what He does, because the questioner has a rank in relation to the one being questioned, and it is customary that the one being questioned is of a lower rank than the questioner. Therefore no one questions Allah, exalted is He, about what He does; as for Him, glorified is He, He questions the people.

For this reason, some witty men (al-Zurafa') said: "The proof that Allah has no partner is that He created so-and-so for such-and-so, because if He had a partner, the partner would have opposed Him in this matter."

So: there is no one higher than Allah, so that one could ask Him, "Why did You do such-and-so?"

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say: Bring your proof. This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me. But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.﴾ (21:24)

Since they have taken gods besides Allah, let them bring proof of their truthfulness. Just as Allah Most High, who is the true God, has brought decisive proofs of His existence, of His power, of His oneness and of His unity, so bring you too what you have. Or are these gods that have no evidence and no proof for them, for He has not sent down a Book, nor sent a messenger, nor brought a method?

Where then are they? If they were not aware of what is happening, then they are heedless gods and it is not right for them to hold this rank. And if they were aware, why did they not confront the realities and defend themselves? Therefore, they are weak in facing this confrontation.

As for His saying, Most High: ﴿Say: Bring your proof...﴾ (21:24) (al-Anbiya’): that is, bring the evidence for the existence of gods other than Allah. The burhan (proof, demonstration) is the indication through the origination of the cosmos in this wondrous order. Have you heard that another god said, "I am the One who originated"? Did he send a messenger with a sign?

Therefore, this is a lying speech, a fabrication and invention from your own selves, because you are not people of knowledge in anything. This does not mean that you deny the existence of knowledge; rather, knowledge exists, but you turn away from hearing it: ﴿But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away﴾ (21:24) (al-Anbiya’).

It is as if the Truth has features they have not learned of. Whoever turns toward seeking the Truth finds it, but whoever turns away from knowledge, from where can he know? Therefore, the Truth exists, and if you sought it you would find it and know it, and grasp the proof for it.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.﴾ (21:25)

So the matter of tawhid (oneness of God) is clear from the beginning of the messages to their conclusion. All of them came with the statement "there is no deity but Allah"; it is a matter shared by all the messages of heaven.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿from a messenger...﴾ (21:25): the "min" (from) here is for comprehensiveness and generality, meaning every individual messenger, everyone who may be called a messenger. If someone says to you, "I have no money," this statement does not prevent him from having a little money, such as coins that are not called money. But if he says, "I do not have any money at all," he has negated the existence of the category of money from the very beginning of what is called money: "I don't have even one millime."

So, what you have brought of the matter of associating partners with Allah, or denying Him, may He be exalted, is a new matter (a fashion) that you have come upon us with.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 26:

His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him...﴾ (26) (al-Anbiya'): That is, exalting Him above having a son. Then say: If He had one, then He has honoured servants, and they are the angels.

Among the attributes of these honoured servants, who are the angels, is that: ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command﴾ (27).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 27:

Although they are honoured servants, they do not precede Him in speech: they do not say what He has not said, nor do they put forward any statement before Him, even if it agrees with the will of God; and they do not do what He has not commanded. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is giving us a sign concerning some of the diseases of society. Among the diseases of society is that you see the great and honoured ones who, from within themselves, create for themselves a temporal authority: they say what their Lord, mighty and majestic, has not said, they do what He has not commanded, and they put their own orders before His orders.

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they act by His command﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:27), meaning: they follow His command; if He commands, they do; if He forbids, they abstain.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive.﴾ (21:28)

The discussion here concerns the honored servants among the angels. Although Allah has honored and favored them, He has not left them without follow-up and observation; rather, He knows what is before them and what is behind them. The matter of intercession has not been left to them so that they may include whomever they love; rather, ﴿they do not intercede except for one whom He approves..﴾ (21:28) (al-Anbiya').

That is: for whom Allah approves and loves. So beware lest you understand that, when you say, "The angels are daughters of Allah," or worship them besides Allah, they will be your intercessors with Allah, because they do not intercede except for those whom Allah loves and approves from among the people of faith. Do not think that they are ﴿honored servants (26)﴾ (al-Anbiya'), meaning: pampered ones who do whatever they please.
