No, they, despite that, are bound by their limits and do not transgress them; for they were not honored with all this honor except because they are obedient and committed.

And they, with this obedience, are ﴿apprehensive out of fear of Him (28)﴾ (al-Anbiya'): so they are not, despite this honor, secure and at ease; rather, they are fearful, anxious, and trembling out of the fear of Allah.

For this reason the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ (21:29)

¹ al-Dahhak said: No angel said that except Iblis; he called to the worship of himself and legislated disbelief. Qatadah said: This was specific to Iblis. (Both cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 5/625).

Meaning: suppose one of them were to say this statement. Then this is a statement that has not happened, and it cannot be said to them: ﴿So We shall recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ (Al-Anbiya). Why? Because they have taken wrongdoing at its highest level, its peak and its extreme arrogance, wrongdoing in the matter of the summit: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great wrong﴾ (Luqman).

Therefore He threatens them, even though they are angels and honoured. But if such a statement should come from any of them, its recompense is Hell, and in this is reassurance for all creation.

After that, the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to demonstrate this oneness which He had affirmed in His previous speech. Oneness (wahdaniyyah) contains within it the quality of being One (ahadiyyah), because there is a difference between them; they are not synonyms as some suppose. Wahid (One) and Ahad (Unique) are two attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say, He is Allah, the One (Ahad)﴾ (Al-Ikhlas), and He said: ﴿the One, the Subduer﴾ (Al-Ra'd).

So wahid means the single individual for whom there is no equal, and this wahid in His essence is ahad, meaning He has no parts. Oneness prevents there being any individual like Him, and absolute uniqueness (ahadiyyah) prevents Him from being composed of parts in His essence; for if He were composed of parts, each part would be dependent for its existence upon the other part, and so He would not be self-sufficient in His existence so as to be a whole. Thus He is neither a universal whole nor a particular part.

For the demonstration, He chose the existing and observable signs of the cosmos, which no one can deny, because they are signs that are orderly, clear and beneficial at the same time. What is seen may be clear yet you have no need of it: a person feels the benefit of the sun if it sets away from him, and feels the benefit of rain if the sky withholds rain, and so on.

Thus the observability of these signs calls for attention to them, and their beneficial character also calls for attention to them, even when they are absent from you, so that you wait and look forward to their return anew.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Have those who disbelieve not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity [ratqan], then We separated them, and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?﴾ (Al-Anbiya 30)

Note on ratq: meaning "joined together" (mar tuqin), i.e. joined in one mass; and with this modern astronomy agrees (Al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/254). Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (6/4459) cites reports from the early scholars on this, among them: (Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, 'Ata', al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: that is, they were one thing, stuck together, and Allah separated them by air).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 30:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have not those who disbelieved considered...? (30)﴾ (al-Anbiya'). He means: have their eyes been blinded, so that they did not look at this universe, wondrous in its making and firm in its engineering and order, and so disbelieve because they were blind to seeing the signs of Allah? And thus, whenever you see the interrogative hamza (همزة) after the waw (واو) and a negated verb, it is to be understood in this way.

But how does the True One, glorified is He, say: ﴿Have not those who disbelieved considered...? (30)﴾ (al-Anbiya'), when the discussion here is about the heavens and the earth, and He has said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor did I take the misguiders as helpers. (51)﴾ (al-Kahf)?

This is a matter that no one witnessed, and no one informed them of it, so how could they see it?

We have previously spoken about "seeing" (al-ru'yah) in the Qur'an, and that it has different usages: sometimes it comes in the sense of "looking" (naẓar), i.e., visual seeing. And it comes in the sense of "knowing" ('ilm), as in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? (1)﴾ (al-Fil).

The Prophet (ﷺ) did not see this event and did not witness it, for he was born in the same year. So the meaning is: "Have you not known?" Then why did the context shift from visual seeing to knowledge-based seeing, even though seeing with the eye is the most emphatic kind of seeing, to the extent that they say: "There is nothing like the eye for certainty"?

They said: Because Allah, may He be exalted, wants to alert His Messenger (ﷺ): you did not see it with your own eyes, but your Lord informed you of it, and the information of Allah is more truthful than the sight of your eyes. So when Allah informs you of something, the information of Allah is more truthful than the sight of the eye. The eye may deceive you, or you may see with it without reflecting. As for the information of Allah to you, it is true and has no deception in it.

Among such uses is also His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with a strong incitement? (83)﴾ (Maryam).

But how was the knowledge-based seeing achieved for them regarding the creation of the heavens and the earth?

They said: Because when a person sees this wondrous universe, he must, even by the instinct of curiosity, ask himself: From where did this marvellous universe come?

A person by nature turns to a wondrous thing and asks about it, even if it does not concern him and does not benefit him. So what about if it is something beneficial to him?

Therefore, it was incumbent on them to consider: who informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of this matter? Especially since they used to ask about it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them with a miracle that proves his truthfulness in conveying from Allah, and informs them of what they were searching for. And since the speech is from Allah, it is true: ﴿And who is more truthful in speech than Allah? (122)﴾ (al-Nisa').

The Qur'an was revealed while in the Arabian Peninsula there were disbelieving idol-worshippers, and in it there were Jews and some Christians, who are People of the Book (ahl al-kitab) who believe in a God, in messengers and in scriptures. To the extent that they used to argue with the pagan disbelievers, saying to them: "The time of a prophet has drawn near whom we will follow, and we will kill you with him, a killing like that of 'Ad and Iram." (1)

Nevertheless, when there came to them what they had recognised of the truth, they disbelieved in it, and aligned themselves with the disbelievers, and became one front and one party with them. What united them was nothing but hatred of the Prophet and of the true religion he brought. And this is similar to what is done today by both the Eastern bloc and the Western bloc, in their alliance against Islam.

So: after Islam came, the People of the Book and the disbelievers became in one trench against Islam. And the disbelievers used to hear from the People of the Book, and in the Torah there is talk about the creation of the heavens and the earth, saying: Allah, when He first created creation, created a jewel. Then He looked at it with a look of awe, and there occurred in it a reaction, vapour and smoke. The smoke rose upward and formed the heaven, and the remainder stayed and formed the earth.

Thus they had a portion of knowledge about the matter of creation. Therefore Allah said about them: ﴿Have not those who disbelieved considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them? (30)﴾ (al-Anbiya').

The orientalists had a discussion regarding His saying: ﴿were a joined mass (30)﴾ (al-Anbiya'). They said: "al-samawat" (the heavens) is a plural, and "al-ard" (the earth) likewise is a collective noun with a plural, so the rule requires that one say "kanna ratqan" with a plural pronoun. The author of this objection did not realise that Allah, may He be exalted, regarded the heaven as a kind and the earth as a kind, so the intended meaning here is the heavenly and the earthly, and these are a dual.

There are many parallels to this matter in the Qur'an, because the Qur'an came in the Arabic style, based on acuteness, intelligence and flexibility of understanding. Take, for example, His saying: ﴿And if two groups of believers fight, then make peace between them... (9)﴾ (al-Hujurat).

He did not say, according to the apparent sense: "iqtatalatā" (they two fought), because the group, although it is singular, contains a multitude, and fighting does not occur between one group and another group, but between the individuals of this one and the individuals of that one. So the fighting takes the plural into account: ﴿...and fight (waqtatalu) (9)﴾ (al-Hujurat). Then when we come to reconciliation, we see that reconciliation is not achieved between these individuals, but between a representative of each group. So reconciliation is established between two sides, and therefore the context returns to the dual: ﴿...then make peace between them. And if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight against the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice... (9)﴾ (al-Hujurat).

The word "ratq" means a thing that is joined and stuck together. The meaning of ﴿...then We parted them (30)﴾ (al-Anbiya') is: We separated them and removed this joining. And what is mentioned in the Torah, that Allah created a jewel, then looked at it with awe, and so on and so forth, the Qur'an has something that supports it in His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly." (11)﴾ (Fussilat).

When scholars encounter a cosmic verse, there are different interpretive positions among them, because it touches on the reality of the universe, and this is a matter open to disagreement. Each of them takes from it according to the measure of his culture and knowledge.

The ancient Arab did not know much about cosmic phenomena. He did not know gravity, nor the sphericity of the earth nor its motion. So if the Qur'an had addressed such matters that his faculties and culture could not encompass, it would perhaps have diverted him by a speech he could not understand. And you can imagine: if you told him, for example, that the earth is a sphere that turns with us, with the seas and mountains upon it, and so on.

The Qur'an is first and foremost a book of method ("do this" and "do not do that"). Therefore, everything relating to this method came clear, with no ambiguity in it. As for cosmic matters, which are subject to human cultures and their civilisational advancement, they came in summary form, awaiting thinking minds that would uncover these phenomena one after another. It is as if the True One, blessed and exalted is He, gives us a mere hint, and it is for contemplative minds to complete this system.

The scholars of Islam had two positions on this matter, both proceeding from love of the religion of Allah, passion for His Book, and a sincere desire to prove the truth of what the Qur'an contains of cosmic signs, which modern science has come to affirm now, although the Qur'an was revealed with them more than fourteen centuries ago.

The first position: its adherents were eager to find for every new discovery a witness from the Qur'an, to say: "The Qur'an preceded it," and that Muhammad (ﷺ) is truthful in his conveyance from Allah.

The second position: as for the proponents of the other position, they were cautious about this matter, fearing that they might assert a theory that has not yet been proven, and seek a witness for it in the Book of Allah, and then it would be shown to be false after they had linked it to the Qur'an.

The correct position is that there is a difference between a scientific theory and a scientific fact. The theory is a matter under investigation and study that has not yet been proven. Therefore they say: "This is theoretical talk," meaning it needs something from reality to support it. As for a scientific fact, it is a matter that has fallen under experiment, its truth has been established empirically, and we are confident that it does not change.

Therefore, it is incumbent upon us not to link the Qur'an to a theory that may be true or false, so that people do not waver in understanding the Qur'an, and accuse us of interpreting the Qur'an according to our desires. But a fixed scientific fact, if it comes in a way that cannot be refuted, there is no objection to linking it to the Qur'an.

An example of this is the matter of the sphericity of the earth. When scholars said it, many objected, raised an uproar, wrote books about it, and some ruled that whoever says this is a disbeliever, because the Qur'an did not explicitly state this matter. But when science advanced, and sufficient evidence for establishing this theory became available, they found the other planets round like the sun and the moon, so why would the earth not be likewise?

Similarly, if you stand, for example, on the sea shore and look at a ship approaching from afar, you see only the top of its sail, and you do not see the rest of the ship until it comes close to you. What does this indicate? This indicates that the surface of the earth is not flat, but has a curvature and bending which indicates its sphericity.

Then, when the age of space came, and scientists ascended into outer space and brought back pictures of the earth, behold, it was indeed round. Thus the theory turned into a scientific fact that cannot be refuted and has no dispute about it, and whoever opposed it when it was a theory now has no choice but to accept it and say it.

What we have said about the sphericity of the earth, we say about its rotation. Who in the past would have believed that the earth is the one that rotates around the sun, with what is upon it of water, buildings and other things? And you may take a jug full of water, tie it with a string from above, then swing it rapidly from below upward, and you will notice that the mouth of the jug is downward without the water spilling. Why? Because the speed of rotation exceeds the gravity of the earth which draws the water towards it. The proof: if you slacken the swinging of the jug, the water falls from its mouth. There must be an effect of gravity, so the gravity of the earth is what holds the water upon it during its rotation.

As for our picking up a theory that is nascent, still under investigation and study, and then rejoicing at linking it to the Qur'an, as happened at the beginning of the modern age and the scientific renaissance, when scientists discovered the solar system, which at its beginning consisted of only seven planets arranged according to their nearness to the sun at the centre: Mercury, then Venus, then Earth, then Mars, then Jupiter, then Saturn, then Uranus.

Here some of our great scholars, among them Shaykh al-Maraghi, hastened to say that these are the seven heavens, and they wrote studies on that, and claimed that the Qur'an had preceded this. Then time passed, and scientists discovered the eighth planet (Neptune), then the ninth (2).

Therefore: linking a theory not yet scientifically confirmed to the Qur'an is a great mistake. And it is possible, if they had more advanced instruments and larger telescopes, as some astronomers say, that they would discover many other planets, because this solar system of ours is one of a hundred million systems in the galaxy which we call Sikkat al-Tabbanah (the Milky Way), and the Greeks call it al-Tariq al-Labani (the Milky Way) (3).

And these planets which we see as big and great, to a degree that exceeds people's imaginings: the sun that we see is larger than the earth by a million and a quarter times (4), and there are planets that could swallow a million suns in their belly.

The distance between us and the sun is eight light-minutes. A light-minute is calculated by multiplying sixty seconds, and the speed of light in one second is 186,000 miles, meaning three hundred thousand kilometres (5).

As for the distance between the earth and the seven-stranded star (al-Muslsalah, i.e., the Pleiades/Sirius region as described), they calculated it in light-years rather than light-minutes, and found it to be a hundred light-years. As for al-Shi'ra (Sirius), which Allah mentioned favourably in His saying: ﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius (49)﴾ (al-Najm), it is even further than that. And all these planets and orbits are in the lowest heaven only, so what has this to do with the seven heavens they have spoken of?

Therefore many admirers of these scientists tried to erase this matter from their books, so that it would not be a disgrace to them and a slip in their scientific path.

Likewise, among the theories they put forward and which missed the truth is their saying: the solar system, including the earth, was formed as a result of the rotation of the sun, which was a blazing mass, so some "fragments" (taratish) separated from it, and some parts came out of it which cooled with the passage of time, and from them the earth was formed. And when...

1 Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of 'Asim ibn 'Amr, on the authority of Qatadah al-Ansari, on the authority of some of their elders, who said: By Allah, concerning us and concerning them, that is, concerning the Ansar and the Jews who were their neighbours, this story was revealed: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them, and previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it... (89)﴾ (al-Baqarah). They said: "We used to dominate them by force for ages in the Jahiliyyah, and we were people of polytheism while they were people of the Book, and they used to say: 'A prophet is about to be sent now, whom we will follow; his time has drawn near, and we will kill you with him, a killing like that of 'Ad and Iram.' But when Allah sent His Messenger from Quraysh and we followed him, they disbelieved in him." Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (1/124).

2 The planet Pluto was not discovered until the year 1930 CE. (Mawsu'at al-Ma'rifah, p. 37).

3 The first to describe the broad band of light known as the Milky Way was Democritus, who held that the Milky Way is composed of a vast number of stars such that no one can distinguish between them, and modern astronomical telescopes have confirmed what he held. (Mawsu'at al-Ma'rifah, p. 5).

4 It is stated in (Mawsu'at al-Ma'rifah) (p. 22): "If the sun were a hollow sphere, it would be able to contain ... 1,300,000 spheres, each of them the size of the earth, before it would be full."

5 That is: the sun is about 94 million miles away from the earth, and its light, which travels at a speed of 186,000 miles per second, reaches us in a little over eight minutes. (Mawsu'at al-Ma'rifah, p. 36).

Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We placed firmly set mountains upon the earth lest it shake with them, and We made in it broad roads as pathways, that they may be guided.﴾

Al-rawasi (the firmly set ones): the mountains, plural of rasi, meaning firmly fixed. He also described them as pegs, saying: ﴿And the mountains as pegs﴾ (al-Naba), likening the mountains in relation to the earth to pegs in relation to a tent.

Then He mentions the reason for this: ﴿lest it shake with them﴾ (al-Anbiya), i.e., lest it incline, be disturbed, and move with them. Had it been created in a state of stability, it would not have shaken or moved, and it would not have needed to be steadied by mountains. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they pass by as the clouds pass by...﴾ (al-Naml).

So it is not strange now that we know the mountains have a motion, even though we do not see it, because they appear stationary relative to our position on them, since we move with the same motion as theirs. It is like you and your companion in a boat, the boat carrying both of you: you do not perceive your companion's motion because you move with the same motion as his.

Allah has likened the motion of the mountains to the passing of clouds. The cloud does not pass by its own inherent motion; rather it passes by the pushing of the winds. Likewise, the mountains do not pass by their own inherent motion but by the motion of the whole earth, and this is a clear proof of the earth's motion.

Then He says, the Exalted: ﴿And We made in it broad roads as pathways﴾ (al-Anbiya), i.e., it is of Allah's wisdom that He made for us in the earth pathways along which we travel. Had the mountains been a mass filling the face of the earth, it would not have been suitable for human life and movement in it. Hence He said: ﴿broad roads as pathways﴾ (al-Anbiya), i.e., wide routes through the valleys and the easy places. In another place He said: ﴿that you may follow therein broad roads﴾ (Nuh).

The meaning of ﴿And We made in it﴾ (al-Anbiya) may apply to the mountains or to the earth; in each there are routes that people travel, and in the mountains they take the form of ravines and valleys.

Then the Exalted mentions the reason for this, saying: ﴿that they may be guided﴾ (al-Anbiya). Guidance here admits two meanings: that they may be guided to their Creator and Maker, and infer from them the Originator, the Exalted; or that they may be guided to towns, places and directions. In antiquity they would take the mountains as signs and landmarks, describing things by their positions relative to the mountains, saying: "The such-and-such place is near the mountain of such-and-such, and on the right of the mountain of such-and-such." Their poet said:

Take the belly of Harsha, or its back, for it,
on both sides of Harsha, has paths for them.

So guidance here includes both this and that, as in His saying: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ (al-Nahl), i.e., they are guided to routes and directions. The Arab would say, for example: "Make the Pleiades on your right, or the Pole Star, or Suhayl, or others," and they had knowledge of the positions of these stars and travelled by their guidance.

Or: they are guided to the fact that the stars have a relation to the life of the living human being. In antiquity they would say: "So-and-so's star has fallen," as if each of us had a star in the sky with some relation to him. Some specialists know this, and perhaps through it they were guided to something, provided they are truthful and trustworthy and do not deceive Allah's creation.

This is supported by His saying: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars, and indeed it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾ (al-Waqi'ah), i.e., if you had knowledge of them, you would know that the stars have a great and mighty role in creation.

1. Al-fajj: the clear, wide road; its plural is fijaj. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/72). Al-fijaj are the paths; al-fajj is the wide road between two mountains. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4462).
2. Harsha: a mountain pass on the Makkah road near al-Juhfah, from which the sea can be seen; it has two routes, and whoever takes either of them is correct. (Lisan al-Arab, root h-r-sh).
3. Ibn Manzur cited this verse in Lisan al-Arab without attributing it to anyone. (Lisan al-Arab, root h-r-sh).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 32:

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾

He called the sky a ceiling (saqf) because the sky is everything that rises above you and shelters you. There is a difference between a ceiling made by human beings, which relies on columns and supports, and so on, and a ceiling made by the Mighty Creator: a ceiling that covers the whole earth and is protected without columns, a level ceiling with no protrusion and no flaw.

The sky has taken on a creative role that God has specified for it, just as He specified Adam, peace be upon him. All creation was created by "Be!" from a father and a mother, but Adam was created directly by the hand of God, glorified is He. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My hands...?"﴾ (38:75). This is a great honour for Adam.

Likewise He said about the creation of the sky: ﴿And the sky We built with might (bi-ayd), and indeed We are its expander.﴾ (51:47).

In another verse He, glorified is He, said: ﴿By the sky having folds (al-hubuk).﴾ (51:7). That is: woven and firmly made. The meaning of hubka is that its particles, which cannot be perceived, are joined together, not a complete joining but a joining of particles. That is why you see the sky as smooth. And therefore the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, said of it: ﴿He raised its height and perfected it.﴾ (79:28).

You may observe human workmanship: when one of us wants to build, for example, or make a ceiling, the building is built with the utmost precision, yet you see one brick protruding beyond another. The plasterer comes and tries to level the wall and checks it with a water level, yet in the wall there are still undulations. Then the painter comes and tries to repair such defects, preparing a filler for them, and it plays an important role in the wall.

After a person has exhausted all his means in preparing his house as it should be, a few days later you see the Truthful, exalted is He, levelling everything and revealing to them the defects of their workmanship, however precise it may be, with a little dust falling vertically, which clearly shows you the defects in the wall.

If human workmanship varies according to the skill and expertise of each person in his work, what then if the craftsman is God, who builds, levels and adorns?

﴿He who created seven heavens in layers. You see no discrepancy in the creation of the Most Merciful.﴾ (67:3).

Now look at the most skilled craftsmen: one levels a ceiling for several rooms, uses one material and colours it with one colour, yet you will inevitably find a difference from one to another. Even if the worker mixes the paint once for all the rooms, the colour comes out different. Why? Because when he takes from this mixture, what remains is more concentrated, and if he does not finish the work on the same day, what is left until the next day loses some water, which also affects the shade of the colour.

And the meaning of ﴿protected (mahfuz)﴾ (21:32): that is, in a formative structure, because it is firm with no difference in it. Only something precious is protected; you guard it because of its preciousness and originality. But from what does God protect it? He protects it from shaking, from falling onto the earth except by His permission.

﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission.﴾ (22:65).

And He said: ﴿And among His signs is that the sky and the earth stand by His command.﴾ (30:25).

Thus, in the creation of the sky there is greatness of creation, greatness of formation, and greatness of preservation befitting His power, exalted is He; none can do it but God. Its maintenance is from Us, and We will not leave you its maintenance, although it needs no maintenance because it is Our workmanship.

Among the matters that the Truthful, exalted is He, has explained to us regarding the sky is the matter of eavesdropping (istiraq al-sam'). The devils used to eavesdrop (yastariqun al-sam') before Islam, but after the mission of Muhammad, peace be upon him, God, glorified is He, willed not to let His call be distorted by a devil's hearing that inspires his enemies. So He prevented the jinn from eavesdropping by means of shooting stars. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We have placed in the sky constellations and adorned it for the beholders. And We have protected it from every accursed devil, except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flame.﴾ (15:16-18).

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿and they turn away from its signs﴾ (21:32): as if the sky had signs specific to it. In the universe there are many signs, and the sky has its signs: the sun, the moon, the stars and the orbits are among its signs.

After that we hear from astronomers that some of the stars' light has not reached us since God created the earth until now, even though the speed of light is three hundred thousand kilometres per second. This can be understood in the light of His saying: ﴿And the sky We built with might, and indeed We are its expander.﴾ (51:47).

Therefore the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, gave us an approximate picture of this matter, so that we do not exhaust ourselves thinking about it: "The seven heavens and the earth, in comparison with the dominion of God, are no more than a ring thrown in a barren desert."(5)

Nevertheless, when the astronauts ascended to the moon, some of our scholars, out of their love for Islam and their sincerity to the Qur'an, hastened to say that they had ascended to the sky, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except with authority.﴾ (55:33).

The intended meaning here is the authority of knowledge that enabled them to ascend.

But since they passed through by the authority of knowledge, why did He say after it: ﴿A flame of fire and brass will be sent against you, and you will not be victorious﴾ (55:35)? So the authority intended is not the authority of knowledge as they imagine; rather it is authority from Me, by My permission and My will.

Had the matter been as they say, they would have said to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, when he told them of the Ascension (mi'raj): "How do you say that, O Muhammad, when your Lord is the one who said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except with authority.﴾ (55:33)?"

Therefore the meaning here is an authority from God, exalted is He, who permits this matter, so that the gates of the sky are opened for him.

Then, what is the connection of the moon with the sky? The discussion concerns passing through the regions of the heavens, and where is the moon in relation to the sky? The distance between the earth and the moon is two light-years; so the moon is nothing but a suburb of the earth, like Maadi, for example, in relation to Cairo. Then what sky is this they speak of?!

As for His saying: ﴿turning away (mu'ridun)﴾ (21:32): we have already discussed i'rad (turning away), which is departing from a thing; from a'rada, meaning he gave it his back.

Notes:
1. Bi-ayd: that is, with strength and power. Said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Thawri and others. Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4/237).
2. That is, He made its ceiling raised and high, or made the distance between it and the earth far. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/399).
3. That is, layer upon layer. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/399). Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/396): (layer after layer; whether they are connected, meaning that the upper ones are on top of one another, or separated with empty space between them? There are two opinions: the more correct is the second, as the hadith of the Night Journey indicates).
4. The Exalted said about the jinn that they said: ﴿And we touched the sky and found it filled with severe guards and flames, and we used to sit in some of its places to listen, but whoever listens now finds a watching flame.﴾ (72:8-9). Ibn 'Abbas said: the devils had seats in the sky where they listened to revelation. When they heard a word, they added to it nine more; the word itself would be true, and what they added would be false. When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was sent, they were prevented from their seats. They mentioned this to Iblis, and before that stars had not been thrown. Iblis said to them: "This matter is nothing but a matter that has occurred on earth." So he sent his soldiers, who found the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, standing and praying between two mountains of a palm grove. They came to him and informed him, and he said: "This is the event that has occurred on earth." Related by al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir and Abu Nu'aym in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/302).
5. Related by Ibn Hibban (94, Mawarid al-Zam'an) from a long hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, in which: "O Abu Dharr, the seven heavens along with the Kursi are nothing but a ring thrown in a barren desert, and the excellence of the Throne over the Kursi is like the excellence of the desert over the ring."
6. Shuwaz: with a dammed or kasra-ed shin, a piece of flame with no smoke in it. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/361).
7. Aqtar: plural of qutr, which is the region and side; so aqtar al-samawat wal-ardh are their regions. (Lisan al-Arab, root q-t-r).

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿It is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit is swimming along.﴾ (21:33)

Al-Haqq, glory be to Him and exalted, bestows favour through some of His creation, and Allah bestows favour only through something great and one of His blessings upon His servants. Among these are the night and the day, and He, glory be to Him, has sworn by them in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears﴾ (Al-Layl).

And He said: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾ (Al-Duha). So the night and the day are two complementary signs, not opposites. Allah created the earth so that His vicegerent might cultivate it: ﴿He produced you from the earth and made you inhabit it...﴾ (11:61) (Hud).

That is: He has asked you to cultivate it with what Allah has given you of the means of life. The directing intellect, the active limbs, the strength and the matter are all created by Allah, the Exalted, and it is incumbent upon you only to use these blessings of Allah in cultivating His earth. When movement is completed in the day, the body then needs rest at night.

Therefore sleep is one of the greatest signs of Allah for man, indicating that the Creator, mighty and majestic, is more trustworthy with the soul than the owner of the soul.

Thus we see some of us exhaust themselves in work and do not give their bodies their natural rest, until they become unable to work and give. Here sleep comes as if it were an inner self-restraint within you, compelling you to rest and sounding the alarm bell for you: you are not fit for work now; have mercy on yourself and give it its right of rest. If you try to sleep before the time of sleep, it refuses you and does not obey you; but when it comes, it takes you from the strongest of influences and overcomes you in everything, so you sleep even on pebbles.

In the Arab proverb: "The bed of the weary is comfortable, and the food of the hungry is delicious." That is: when a weary, exhausted person sleeps, he sleeps even on pebbles, without any means of comfort, and yet sleeps a restful sleep.

And in another proverb: "Sleep is a guest: if you seek it, it helps you; if it seeks you, it refreshes you." Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, speaks to us of the sign of sleep in another place: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day...﴾ (30:23) (Al-Rum).

Here is a precaution and a remark: if sleep at night is for tranquillity and rest, there are those who work at night and sleep by day, such as guards, police officers, bakers and others, and there is no objection to these sleeping by day so that they keep pace with the movement of life.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿And the sun and the moon...﴾ (21:33) (Al-Anbiya). Yes, there are many other signs in Allah's creation, but the clearest and most well-known are the sun and the moon, for they are under observation. ﴿Each in an orbit is swimming along﴾ (21:33) (Al-Anbiya). So the night, the day, the sun and the moon each revolve after the other and succeed it, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day succeed each other...﴾ (25:62) (Al-Furqan).

The word ﴿yasbahun﴾ (they swim, 21:33) (Al-Anbiya) is a precise Qur'anic expression for the manner of motion. It is derived from the swimming of a fish in water, where the fish glides through the softness of the water with an easy, flowing motion, because movement to cover distances is either flowing motion or leaping motion.

You can observe these two kinds of motion in the hands of a clock. If you observe the second hand, for example, you will find that it moves in a leaping motion: it moves from rest to motion to rest. Time, then, has a part for motion and a part for stillness. The minute hand, however, moves with a continuous flowing motion: every part of time contains a part of motion. Thus is the swimming of the fish, and among its examples is His saying: ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾ (79:3) (Al-Nazi'at).

Likewise is the movement of a shadow: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow...﴾ (25:45) (Al-Furqan). Also the movement of a child's growth: if you gaze continuously at your little child, you can hardly notice signs of growth on him, as if he were not growing before your eyes; but if you are absent from him for, say, several months, you can notice his growth. That is because growth is a motion distributed over every second of time, not that growth gathers and then appears suddenly.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you immortality. So if you die, would they be immortal?﴾

That is because the disbelievers attempted to kill the Prophet (ﷺ) by dropping a stone on him from a high place, and this is how they would be rid of him (ﷺ). They used to wish for that. So his Lord addressed him: "O Muhammad, you are no novelty among the Messengers. ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die.﴾" (az-Zumar).

This is the sunnah of Allah in His creation. Moreover, your death, O Muhammad, is to hasten your reward for what you bore of the hardships of the call and the toil of this worldly life.

Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given the choice regarding death, he said: "Rather, the Highest Companion" (al-rafiq al-a'la). As for us, we cling to life and seek to prolong it.

So His saying, ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you immortality...﴾ (al-Anbiya'): you are like others among humankind before you, and those after you will not be immortal after death. ﴿So if you die, would they be immortal?﴾ (al-Anbiya'): so let them not rejoice at your death, for they are not immortal after you.

1 The Jews of Banu al-Nadir came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to help him pay the blood-money (diyya) for two slain men. They said: "We will help you in what you wish, in what you have sought our help for." Then some of them withdrew together and said: "You will not find the man in a situation like this" (while the Messenger of Allah was sitting beside a wall of their houses). "Who will climb onto this house and drop a rock on him, to rid us of him?" 'Amr ibn Jihash volunteered for this and said: "I will do it." He climbed up to drop a rock on him, but the news of what the people intended came to the Messenger of Allah from heaven, so he stood up and left, returning to Madinah. He (ﷺ) then ordered preparations for fighting them and marching against them. (Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham, 3/3/190).

2 Imam Ahmad recorded it in his Musnad (6/274) from the hadith of 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say often, I heard him say: 'Allah does not take a prophet until he is given the choice.'" She said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was near death, the last word I heard from him was him saying: 'Rather, the Highest Companion from Paradise.'"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 35:

Idhan (so, then): death is a universal law applying to everyone, and in its reality it is good. If they were good people, We hasten their reward to them with Allah; and if they were evil, Allah has relieved the lands and the servants of them.

But how is death "tasted"? Dhawq (tasting) here means a person's feeling of pain from death. If a person has actually died, it is impossible for him to taste it. Rather, before dying, he tastes the preliminaries of death. The poet says:

"And grief after the separation of the soul is impotence,
and grief does not occur before the parting."

So at what does a person grieve after he has died? And why would grief come before he dies?

Therefore, what is meant, then, is one who tastes the preliminaries of death, by which he knows that he is dying. A person, however healthy he may be, must inevitably reach a time when he realizes that he is certainly dying. That is when the soul reaches the collarbone (al-halqum, the throat), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No! When it reaches the collarbones, and it is said, "Who will heal him?" and he thinks that it is the parting﴾ (Al-Qiyamah 26-28). Death in this state is a settled matter.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ (Al-Anbiya 35). That is: We test you. Testing (ibtila', trial) is not blameworthy in itself; what is blameworthy is its ultimate purpose: Will one succeed in it or fail? Just as we test students: is the examination at the end of the year an evil? But does Allah, the Truthful, need to test His servants in order to know their condition? The Truth tests creation not in order to know, but in order to establish the proof against them.

The addressee in ﴿We test you﴾ (Al-Anbiya 35) is everyone: the rich and the poor, the healthy and the sick, the ruler and the ruled, and so on.

So: we are all a trial for one another. The rich is a trial for the poor, and the poor is a trial for the rich. How? The poor: will he endure his poverty and be content with it, or will he harbor resentment and envy toward the rich, or will he say, "Bismillah, mashallah, O Allah, bless him, and give me of Your goodness"? The rich: will he conduct his wealth well, paying its due and spending from it on the needy?

Thus, you can run such comparisons to learn that evil and good are both a trial and a test, which ends either in success or in failure. Therefore He says after it: ﴿And to Us you will be returned﴾ (Al-Anbiya 35), so that We may recompense each one for his deeds. If success accompanies you, then for you is the reward and recompense; and if you fail, then for you is punishment. The matter must end with a return to Allah.

Then the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted One says:

﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in mockery: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾ (21:36)

This is an address to the Messenger of Allah concerning an event that happened to him with the disbelievers: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in mockery...﴾ (al-Anbiya). The particle (in) here is not conditional; rather it is for negation, as in His saying: ﴿Those of you who divorce their wives by zihar—they are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who bore them...﴾ (al-Mujadila 58:2). That is: their mothers are none but those who bore them.

So the meaning is: when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in mockery, i.e., they ridicule you. But what is the nature of the mockery here?

Their saying: ﴿"Is this the one who mentions your gods...?"﴾ (al-Anbiya): that is, he disparages them and reviles them, and says of them that they are false. And the phrase ﴿"Is this..."﴾ (al-Anbiya): it is as if they belittle him, and belittle that he should say this about their gods.

Mention (dhikr) may be with good and may be with evil. If a friend mentions you, you expect him to mention you with good; and if an enemy mentions you, you expect him to mention you with evil. And since Muhammad would mention their gods, he would certainly mention them with evil. The evil that Muhammad mentioned about your gods was that they are idols and stones that neither harm nor benefit:

﴿If you call upon them, they do not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association...﴾ (Fatir 35:14).

Then He says, Exalted: ﴿And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾ (al-Anbiya 21:36). So how do you marvel and become angry that Muhammad reviles your false gods, while you revile the True God and disbelieve in Him? We note that the context mentioned the pronoun referring to them twice: ﴿And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers﴾ (al-Anbiya 21:36), to emphasize that this occurred from them.

1 Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by Abu Sufyan and Abu Jahl while they were conversing. When Abu Jahl saw him he laughed and said to Abu Sufyan: 'This is the prophet of the Banu Abd Manaf.' Abu Sufyan became angry and said: 'Do you deny that the Banu Abd Manaf may have a prophet?' The Prophet (ﷺ) heard them, so he returned to Abu Jahl, confronted him, and threatened him, saying: 'You will not desist until there befalls you what befell your uncle.' And he said to Abu Sufyan: 'As for you, you did not say what you said except out of partisanship.'" Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in mockery................(36)﴾ (al-Anbiya). [The verse.] Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/630).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 37:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten.﴾

The meaning of ﴿of haste (min ʿajal)﴾ (al-Anbiya): that is, he is hasty, as if haste were in his very clay. Haste (ʿajala) is wanting a thing before it has ripened and before its appointed time. A person may hasten toward good, and this is permissible; but to hasten toward evil is sheer folly and stupidity. Did they not say to the Messenger of Allah: ﴿When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?﴾ (al-Anbiya)?

Did they not say: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment﴾ (al-Anfal)?

So these people hastened the punishment because they do not believe in it, and do not accept that any of this will come to pass; therefore He answers them: ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten﴾ (al-Anbiya). And He addressed His Prophet (ﷺ) with His words: ﴿Whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), to Us they will return﴾ (Ghafir).

That is: We will show you among them Our signs, and you will see what We have promised them of punishment; and if We take you to Us, you will see what befalls them in the Hereafter.

1 That is: the nature of man is haste, so he hastens toward many things even when they are harmful. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi, 6/4465)

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And they say, "When will this promise be, if you are truthful?"﴾

This is their impatience regarding Allah's promise of the Hereafter and its presentation before Him, glory be to Him, and that He will punish them with the Fire that scorches their skins, and Allah will replace their skins with other skins... etc. This is because they do not believe this and do not accept it. And they had earlier said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿"Or you cause the heaven to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee"﴾ (al-Isra').

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to keep the Fire from their faces, nor from their backs, nor will they be helped﴾ (21:39).

That is: if only they knew what will happen to them at this time, when they will be unable to ward off the Fire from their faces. The face is mentioned in particular because it is the noblest and most honoured of a human being's limbs. That is why, if harm reaches your face, you are eager to remove it with your hand, though all you have done is move the harm from your face to your hand. Why? Because the face is precious to you; you do not accept its humiliation and you do not bear any evil upon it.

So His saying ﴿nor from their faces the Fire﴾ (21:39) indicates their humiliation; ﴿nor from their backs﴾ (21:39) because it comes at them from every direction; and ﴿nor will they be helped﴾ (21:39), meaning they will find no one to rescue them or take them by the hand and ward off the Fire from them.

Even Satan, who led them astray and enticed them in the world, will disown them on the Day of Resurrection and say: ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾ (14:22). The verb "aṣrakhahu" (to cry out to someone, i.e., to answer his cry for help) comes from "ṣarakha," and the hamza in "aṣrakhahu" is called the hamzat izalah (the hamza of removal), as in: "ṣarakha fulān" when something falls upon a person that is beyond his strength and endurance, so he cries out, calling for one who will relieve and help him. If the one called answers and removes what he is in, then he has "aṣrakhahu," meaning he removed the cause of his crying out. So the meaning is: I do not defend you, nor do you defend me; I do not rescue you from the punishment, nor do you rescue me.

In another place: ﴿Like Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, [Satan] says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ (59:16). The share of Satan is to plunge you into disobedience, and then to disown you.

What is the response (jawab) of "law" here? The meaning: if those who disbelieve knew the time when the Fire will not be kept from their faces or their backs and they will not be helped, they would withdraw from what leads them to that, and desist from its causes.

Then the Truthful, Exalted One says: ﴿Nay, it will come upon them suddenly, and it will confound them, so they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be granted respite﴾ (40).

That is: the Resurrection (al-qiyamah). "Al-baghtah" (suddenness) is the arrival of an event before one expects it. ﴿Fa-tabhituhum﴾ (40) (from Surat al-Anbiya): from "al-baht," meaning astonishment and bewilderment. So when the Resurrection overtakes them, they are astonished and bewildered, not knowing what to do, or where to flee.

Suddenness prevents preparation and readiness, and prevents the safeguarding of the self.

An example of this is what people used to do during wartime with air-raid sirens, which alert people to the occurrence of an air raid, for instance. People then prepare themselves and take refuge in shelters. But if the enemy surprises them suddenly, they will not be able to do that, and will find no opportunity to escape the danger.

Among the uses of "baht" is the Most High's saying in the story of the one who argued with Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about his Lord: ﴿...Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." So the one who disbelieved was confounded...﴾ (258) (Surat al-Baqarah).

As for His saying ﴿nor will they be granted respite﴾ (40) (Surat al-Anbiya): that is, they will not be given time or delay. The matter is not a threat after which We turn away from them to another time; rather, it is the great seizing that will not be averted from them or postponed.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And mockery was certainly made of messengers before you, but there descended upon those who mocked them that which they used to ridicule.﴾

Earlier, Allah Almighty addressed His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in ridicule...﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 36). Therefore, He consoles him here: you are not unprecedented among the messengers. So take this matter with an open chest, for messengers before you were mocked. Do not grieve, for what they have done will befall them, and they will find the consequence of this mockery.

Likewise, in the story of Noah, peace be upon him, it came: ﴿And he was constructing the ship, and every time a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him...﴾ (Hud, 38). Noah replied: ﴿If you mock us, then indeed we mock you as you mock [us].﴾ (Hud, 38). That is: wait for the end, and you will see!

As for the meaning of "fa-haqa" (﴿فَحَاقَ﴾, Al-Anbiya', 41): it means it descended and came down with severity upon ﴿those who mocked them, that which they used to ridicule.﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 41).

This meaning is clear in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they exchanged winks. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are [really] astray." But they had not been sent as observers over them. So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, [reclining] on adorned couches, looking. Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ (Al-Mutaffifin, 29–36). That is: joyful and delighted. This is evidence of their meanness and the baseness of their natures. They were not content with mockery, but would imitate it and boast of it.

Have we been able to repay them for what they did? Yes, O Lord.

We must not forget that the mockery of the disbelievers toward the people of truth is limited to its time in this world, whereas Allah's mockery of them is everlasting, without end. Here we must take heed of this matter: the people of faith often suffer mockery and ridicule from the people of falsehood, and those who mock them for their sake, Allah preserves life for them and repels punishment from them, as came in the hadith qudsi: (Were it not for infants nursing, elders bowing, and animals grazing, I would have poured down punishment upon you in a torrent.)¹ ²

So when you see a pious person, if you do not thank him for his piety and follow his example, then at least leave him to his state: do not ridicule him or mock him, for in his existence is the preservation of your life and your security. The least you can do to honor piety is that you be safe from his evil; he will not transgress against you, and you will not see from him anything that grieves you.

¹ "Al-Ra'ta" (al-rat'): grazing in fertile land; "rata'at al-mashiyah" means the livestock ate what they wished and came and went in the pasture by day. (Lisan al-Arab, root r-t-a)
² Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/227) from a hadith of Abu Hurayrah, attributing it to al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, except that he said: (Were it not for youths humbled, elders bowing, infants nursing, and animals grazing, the punishment would have been poured upon you in a torrent.) In its chain is Ibn Khaytham, who is weak.

Then the Truly Majestic (Allah, glorified and exalted) says: ﴿Say: "Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?" Nay, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾ (42)

Meaning: who guards you and preserves you. It is as if Allah, glorified and exalted be He, is drawing a comparison between His favour upon His servants and what they return to Him of denial, ingratitude and disbelief. You disbelieve in Allah, harm the righteous among His servants, and mock them, while it is He who ﴿protects you by night and by day﴾ (Al-Anbiya): that is, a protection issuing from Allah, the Most Merciful.

This is like His saying: ﴿They guard him by the command of Allah﴾ (Ar-Ra'd, 11). The meaning is not that they guard him from the command of Allah which Allah has willed concerning him, because the guarding issues from Allah, and the guardians are charged by Him, exalted be He, with guarding you, and it is not a voluntary act on their part. Allah's protection of you and His preserving you by day and by night, while you sleep, are guardians who watch over you and ward off harm from you.

We often hear that some people rise from their sleep and find a serpent in their bed, yet it did not harm them, and perhaps they were terrified at the sight of it and suffered harm because of this fear, not knowing that a serpent does not harm a person as long as he does not bother it. This is one of the wonders of these creatures: they do not harm you so long as you do not harm them.

So, no one watches over you and guards you from what would harm you during your sleep except Allah, glorified be He.

Allah's protection of you is not limited to safeguarding you from ruin. Among His protection, glorified be He, is that He supplies you with the means of life: the sun with its light, the moon with its radiance, the earth with its plants, and the sky with its water. Despite this, you disbelieve in Him and mock His messengers and the people of His obedience. Therefore He says after it: ﴿Nay, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾ (Al-Anbiya, 42)

And it would not be correct that His remembrance be absent from them.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? They are unable to help themselves, nor can they be accompanied by Us (i.e., be protected by Us).﴾

Do they have other gods that prevent them from believing in God? These gods are unable to help themselves. How could they help themselves, when they are idols of stone, carved by their worshippers into forms they chose? How could they help themselves? If the wind were to knock one of them over, it would need someone to lift it up and set it upright.

As for His saying, ﴿nor can they be accompanied by Us﴾ (al-Anbiya': 43): In former times, in the desert, when one of them committed a sin, or did a deed against one of the tribes, and needed to pass through their territory on his journey, he would go to a strong man who would accompany him on his journey and protect him from them until he had passed through their dwellings, as in His saying: ﴿And they have a charge against me, so I fear that they will kill me﴾ (al-Shu'ara': 14).

The meaning, then, is: he seeks a companion so that the companionship will protect him and he will be saved from punishment. So, these (idols) will not be in companionship with us so as to save them, nor can anyone accompany them to save them from Our punishment. Neither this nor that.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Nay, We gave these people and their fathers enjoyment until life was long upon them. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? Are they then the victors?﴾ (21:44).

Meaning: they remained for a long period of time, living in the blessings of Allah. But look at what happened to them afterward, and take a lesson from them: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength, and they tilled the earth and populated it more than these have populated it...﴾ (30:9).

Yet they were seized with the seizure of the Mighty, the Able, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established in the land as We have not established you, and We sent down the sky upon them in abundant rain and made rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and brought into being after them another generation﴾ (6:6).

Then He, glorified be He, says: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts...﴾ (21:44), and in another place: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning﴾ (13:41).

This is one of the verses at which some of our scholars who are concerned with the scientific miracles of the Qur'an have paused. When scientists announced that the earth is egg-shaped (ellipsoidal) and not perfectly round, meaning that its diameters differ with respect to its center, some hastened, out of zeal for the religion of Allah and in an attempt to prove the truth of the Qur'an and that it had preceded to mention this matter, saying: The Qur'an mentioned this discovery in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts...﴾ (21:44). That is: from the direction of the equator, not from the direction of the poles.

But these people overlooked that the verse says: ﴿reducing it from its outlying parts...﴾ (21:44), not "from its outlying part," so the reduction is from all the outlying parts. Such statements open the door to disparaging the Qur'an and to meddling with it.

We ask: ﴿Do they not see...﴾ (21:44): is "see" here a knowledge-seeing (ʿilmiyyah) or a sight-seeing (baṣariyyah)? If we say it is sight-seeing, then this is a phenomenon that was not known until the twentieth century, and no one noticed it before that; therefore it is not sight-seeing. Nor is it knowledge-seeing, for this information did not reach these people, and the Arabs at that time were not a people of knowledge, nor a people of culture, nor anything of the sort at all. So if we set aside this interpretation, what is the appropriate meaning?

We say: if "saw" is sight-seeing, then they saw this phenomenon among the earlier nations, and they were opposing the religion of Allah and fighting it, because it came to end their temporal authority and to make people equal; yet despite that, the religion spread every day, its domain grew, and the domain of disbelief shrank.

So the meaning is: We reduce the land of disbelief, either by its people or by the buildings that are destroyed and ruined by earthquakes, landslides and other things. Thus We reduce the land, We reduce the people, and We reduce the manifestations of civilization on the side of disbelief, and this reduction is itself an increase in the land of faith.(3) And this phenomenon occurred in all the messages.

If someone says: how can we accept this interpretation, when the increase of the land of faith only happened after the Hijrah, and the verse is Meccan? We say: that the verse is Meccan does not undermine the meaning here, for it is not necessary that they see it in themselves; it suffices that they see it in the earlier nations, as Allah said: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ (37:137).

And He said: ﴿And Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh, owner of stakes, who had transgressed in the lands and increased therein corruption﴾ (89:9–12).

And if we consider "saw" to be knowledge-seeing, then they learned of that from the People of the Book with whom they were allied, so what happened to the earlier nations will happen to you.

As for His saying: ﴿Then are they the victors?﴾ (21:44): that is, did they not witness that We reduce the land from its outlying parts, or is it that this has not happened and they are the victors? Which is victorious: the messengers of Allah or the disbelievers? The answer is that they were overcome and routed. So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they will be the victorious﴾ (37:173), and He said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world...﴾ (40:51).

1 *Atharal-ard*: plowing, splitting and turning the earth for cultivation or other purposes, such as extracting minerals or extracting water. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/113).
2 *Qarn*: the people who come after a people; a qarn of people are the inhabitants of one era. Al-Azhari said: "What appears to me, and Allah knows best, is that the qarn is the people of every city in which there was a prophet or in which there was a class of scholars; whether the years were few or many." (Lisan al-Arab, root q-r-n).
3 Ibn 'Abbas said: "Did they not see that We open the land to Muhammad ﷺ, land after land?" Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: it is the victory of the Muslims over the polytheists. 'Ikrimah said: "If the land were being reduced, you would not find a place to sit, but it is death." Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2/520): "The first opinion is more preferable, and it is the victory of Islam over polytheism, town after town; and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir."

Almighty Allah addresses His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "I only warn you by revelation, but the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned."﴾

That is, the Messenger of Allah did not convey to you anything from himself. Everything he brought, whether promise or threat, is from Allah. You yourselves insist on his humanity: yes, he is a human being who knows nothing, as you say, and this counts in his favour, not against him, for it is his Lord who reveals to him.

So if Muhammad had said, "I warn you...", you would have had a right to doubt. But the one who speaks is Allah, and I am merely a messenger conveying from Allah, who controls the reins of events. When He announces that an event will occur, it must happen.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿and the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned﴾ (al-Anbiya').

The sense of hearing is the first of a human being's perceptions and the first of his senses to function. Before a child speaks, he must first hear in order to reproduce what he has heard, because hearing is the first perception accompanying the formation of perceptions, and the ear, as we have said, precedes the eye in performing its task.

Therefore Almighty Allah gave it precedence, saying: ﴿Indeed, the hearing and the sight and the heart – all of those will be questioned about﴾ (al-Isra'). 

Hearing is the faculty that never ceases its task, even when a person is asleep, because through it summoning takes place. So when Almighty Allah willed to put the People of the Cave to sleep for that long period, He struck upon their ears and disabled their sense of hearing, so that the sounds of nature outside the cave would not disturb them. He said: ﴿So We struck upon their ears in the cave for a number of years﴾ (al-Kahf: 11).

As for the meaning of ﴿the deaf do not hear the call...﴾ (al-Anbiya': 45): it is true that they do hear, and their hearing apparatus is capable of functioning, but it is a hearing without benefit. The benefit of hearing is that you respond to the one who speaks to you; if you do not respond, it is as if you had not heard. If you tell a worker something, for example, and he ignores it, you say to him, "Are you deaf?" That is why the Qur'an calls them "deaf."

As for His saying: ﴿when they are warned﴾ (al-Anbiya': 45): that is, they are indifferent to an ordinary call, and they turn away, but [it is] when they are warned of Allah's punishment [that they are most indifferent]. Warning and caution are among the things a person most ought to attend to, for in them lies his own benefit, and it is foolish not to attend to them. It is like when you warn a person and caution him about the dangers of a road, that there are wolves, lions, snakes or highwaymen on it, and he pays no heed to your words and takes no precaution to save himself.

We have said that warning (indhar) is to tell a person of an evil before its time, so that he may prepare to avert it, not to warn him at the moment of the event when he finds no opportunity.

So the matter is not a natural defect in creation, but a turning of perception: like when you speak to someone about a matter he does not like, and you find him (deaf as a post, deaf as a stone), turning away from you as if he had heard nothing. Like the man who said to his companion, "Is there among you someone who keeps secrets?" He said, "Yes, your secret is in a well." He said, "Give me ten pounds." He replied, "As if I had heard nothing!!"

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they would surely say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾

Only now do you pay attention and understand? Only now, after the punishment has touched them?

As for the meaning of ﴿a breath of the punishment of your Lord should touch them﴾ (al-Anbiya': 46): that is, a touch, a light brushing. The nafhah (a light breath, a gentle scent) is the soft wind that carries to you the traces of things without their reality. For example, the wind may carry to you the fragrance of roses: it does not carry the roses themselves, only their scent, while the roses remain as they are.

Likewise, this touch of punishment is merely a scent of punishment, like the scorching heat of fire that we feel while we are far from it.

And nafhah is a noun of single occurrence (ism marrah), meaning that it indicates that it happened once, just as you say jalasa jalsah, meaning once. This is also a proof of minimization.

The word "touched" (massathum) is a minimization, the word "breath" (nafhah) is a minimization, and its being a single occurrence is another minimization. Yet even so, they cry out and wail, so what would they do if the punishment came down upon them in its true reality, which is an everlasting punishment?

As for His saying, ﴿they would surely say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers"﴾ (al-Anbiya': 46): now they speak; now they say the word of truth which they had long concealed. Now their sensitivity of perception appears, for at the least touch, at the mere scent of punishment, they cry out. And where was this perception and this sensitivity before? So the matter, as we have said, is not a matter of natural constitution, but a matter of directing perceptions.

As for their words, ﴿Woe to us!﴾ (al-Anbiya': 46): this is an awareness of what they are about to face, and this utterance issues from sensations in the soul and mind before the word is spoken. Then they acknowledge against themselves and confess: ﴿Indeed, we were wrongdoers﴾ (al-Anbiya': 46).

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 21, verse 47

God, glorified and exalted, moves them from denial, rejection, and mockery of the Messenger's words, from their refusal to believe in revelation, and from their deafness to goodness, to the matter of the reckoning and the just balance. Why this shift? To alert them and draw their attention to the fact that this message, which they met with denial and doubt, was for their own benefit, and that everything is reckoned and will be weighed against them and counted. It is as if He were advising them. Thus God's mercy toward them and His concern for their salvation continue.

The word (mawazin, "balances") is the plural of (mizan, "balance"), an instrument by which things are measured in terms of their density. Measurement occurs in several respects: density by weight, distances by measurement, and so on. People have set fixed standards for these measures. For example, the metre was made of platinum so that it would not corrode, and it is currently kept, roughly, in Paris, and likewise the yard. For weight they made standards of iron: the kilogram and the pound, and so on.

In earlier times they would weigh a piece of stone equal to one kilogram, for example, and use it for weighing, because it had a reference point. But this piece wears away through frequent use, so it must be replaced.

Here God speaks of the thing that is weighed and does not mention the other standards. Some said: because things that have density are the most common. They used to test children, asking: "Is a kilogram of iron heavier, or a kilogram of cotton?" The child looks at the cotton and sees it as fluffy and puffed up, and says: "The cotton." Cotton is indeed larger than iron in volume, but its density can be reduced; we can flatten the cotton until it becomes an area of length and width. So the basis of measurement is weight.

In another place God the Exalted says: ﴿And the heaven He raised, and He set up the balance﴾ (Al-Rahman, 55:7). Are these multiple balances, or is it one balance?

All of creation will be reckoned at one time. They will not stand in a queue, each waiting for his turn, but all at once. For this reason, when Imam Ali, may Allah honor his face, was asked: "How does God reckon all of creation at one time?" he said: "Just as He provides for them all at one time." The matter is difficult for you, but for God, the Exalted, it is easy and simple.

Al-qist is an attribute of the balances; it is a verbal noun meaning justice, as you say in praising a judge: "This is a just judge" (qadi 'adil), meaning one described by justice. If you want to intensify, you say: "This is a judge of justice" (qadi 'adl), as if he himself were justice, i.e., "kneaded with justice." For this reason we say of God's names: "al-Hakam al-'Adl" (the Judge, the Just), and we do not say: "al-'Adil."

This root (q-s-t) has a role in the language: it is one of the homonymous words that carry both a meaning and its opposite, like (zawj, "spouse/pair"), which is applied to both man and woman, and (ayn, "eye"), which is applied to the seeing eye, to the spring of water, to the spy, and to gold and silver.

Likewise, (al-qist) with a kasra (qisṭ) means justice, from qasata qistan (he acted justly), as in God's words: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ (Al-Ma'idah, 5:42). And we say (al-qast) with a fatha means injustice, from qasata qusuwwan and qasatan (he acted unjustly), as in God's words: ﴿And as for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell﴾ (Al-Jinn, 72:15), that is, the tyrannical and wrongdoing.

Qist in the sense of justice means that one rules justly from the outset. But aqsata means that there was an unjust ruling and he corrected it into a just ruling on appeal.

From the same root is God's saying: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah﴾ (Al-Ahzab, 33:5). Here "aqsaṭ" is the comparative form, indicating that the ruling of Muhammad (ﷺ) in the matter of Zayd was just and equitable, but the ruling of his Lord, the Exalted, is more just and more equitable.

It is known from the story of Zayd ibn Harithah that he preferred the Messenger of God and chose him over his family. It was natural for the Messenger of God to reward him for his love and sincerity and to compensate him for his family, whom the Messenger had set aside. The reward was that he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad.

So: God is just toward His Messenger, but it is a justice that is not oppression. God's justice is more excellent than Muhammad's justice. For this reason He said: ﴿more just in the sight of Allah﴾ (Al-Ahzab, 33:5). As for you, in your view, Muhammad made an extreme of justice.

As for God's saying: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾ (Al-Ahzab, 33:5), it came to nullify adoption, so that this would be a prelude to new legislation concerning the family, marriage, the prohibited degrees, and many other matters in God's law, which cannot stand while this practice exists. Otherwise, what would be the situation of the family when the adopted son grows up and reaches manhood? What would his position be toward the wife and the daughter, when in reality he is a stranger to the family?

This matter of the balances is among those in which the orientalists found a contradiction in the apparent meaning of the verses, and they made it an objection against the Book of God. Among this is their claim of contradiction between the two verses: ﴿And We set up the balances of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:47), and His saying: ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (Al-Kahf, 18:105). In the first, He affirms the balance, and in the second He negates it.

We have said that these people are excused, because they do not possess the linguistic competence that would enable them to understand the words of God. If we reflect on the lam in ﴿We will not give them﴾ (Al-Kahf, 18:105), this difficulty is resolved: the lam indicates ownership and benefit, as they say in the language of banks: "له وعليه" (for him and against him). The Qur'an says: ﴿For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 2:286).

So the meaning of ﴿We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (Al-Kahf, 18:105) is: no weight in their favor. Rather, We will set up (the balance) against them and judge them. Likewise, we find that the word "weight" (wazn) is used in the language either for material weight or for weight of meaning, as we say: "So-and-so has no weight among men."

On this basis the meaning is: they have no weight in their persons and their substance; the weight belongs to their deeds. We do not say, "He was among the notables" or "his origin was such-and-such." This matter is clear in the story of the son of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿He said: "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, his work was unrighteous"﴾ (Hud, 11:46).

So the sonship here is sonship of deed and faith, not sonship of essence.

The disbelievers and the disobedient have supposed that they have weight with God and a rank that will be theirs in the Hereafter, as it was theirs in this world. This is as in the story of the owner of the two gardens, who said to his companion, boasting and proud: ﴿I have more wealth than you and greater support in men.﴾ And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said: "I do not think this will ever perish. And I do not think the Hour will occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination" (Al-Kahf, 18:34–36).

But it is far-fetched that they should have weight in the Hereafter. The weighing on the Day of Resurrection is for deeds, not for persons.

So the meaning is: We do not weigh their persons; We weigh their deeds. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his kinsmen: (No people will come to me with their deeds while you come to me with your lineages.)<sup>(2)</sup>

And he (ﷺ) said: (O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, work, for I cannot avail you anything against God.)<sup>(3)</sup>

So essences, lineages, and ancestries have no value in this situation.

As for God's saying: ﴿So no soul will be wronged in the least﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:47). Although the principle is: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 2:194), these people have greatly wronged God, the Exalted, by associating others with Him, and they wronged the Messenger of God by saying of him: "a magician," "a liar," and "a madman." Nevertheless, We will not repel this transgression with the like of their wrongdoing.

And His saying: ﴿And even if it should be the weight of a mustard seed, We would bring it forth﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:47). The mustard seed is an example of smallness, to indicate the thoroughness of accounting for everything. The mustard seed is still the global standard for the kilogram: they found that mustard seeds are equal in weight, so they took from them the unit of the kilogram now.
