So the method he brought, which strips these civilizations of their might and glory, must necessarily be a method higher than all these methods and civilizations.

Then He (exalted is He) says: ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾ (92) [al-Anbiya']: that is, adhere to My method so that you remain one community. He chose the attribute of lordship and did not say "your God," because the Lord is the One who created, provided and nurtured, whereas the God (ilah) is the One who imposes obligations.

The meaning: since I am your Lord who created you from non-existence, and sustained you from non-existence, and I am the Sustainer over your interests, guarding you by night and day, and I provide even for the disobedient and the one who disbelieves in Me, then I am more worthy of worship, and it is not fitting for you that I do all this for you and you go off to a god other than Me. This is the logic of sound reason, and as they say: "Whoever eats my bread hears my word."

Among worship is obeying God in His commands and prohibitions, because the fruit of this obedience returns to you as benefit. God (exalted is He) possesses the attributes of eternal perfection before He created one who obeys Him, so your obedience will add nothing to God's dominion, and your disobedience will diminish nothing from it. Therefore the matter returns to you, and your Lord rewards you for an act which in truth is for your own good.

But did people hear this call and act upon its requirement, so that they became one community like this community which brought the world into the embrace of Islam within half a century? This is the community whose effect we still see in the lands that rebelled against Arabism and the language of the Qur'an, yet they are Muslims in their own languages and their own civilizations. The religion that produces this, and the one community that bore this responsibility, should not be abandoned by us.

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4519): "When He mentioned the prophets, He said: these all agree upon monotheism, so ummah here means the religion, which is Islam. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others."
2 A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3535) and Muslim in his Sahih (2286), Kitab al-Fada'il (hadith 22), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).
3 Ibn Mas'ud was asked: what is the ummah? He said: the one who teaches people goodness. Qatadah said: a leader of guidance who is followed and whose sunnah is pursued. [al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 5/176].

Question: Did the single community remain? The verses answer:

﴿And they cut their affair among themselves into sects; to Us they will all return.﴾ (21:93)

That is: they became factions, parties, groups and sects, as the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects — you are not [associated] with them in anything.﴾ (6:159)

Why "you are not [associated] with them in anything"? Because they undermine the oneness of the community, and the community's oneness is undermined only when it differs, and it differs only when its methods are many. Here disagreement arises; but if they all proceed from one method, they will not differ.

Since they have cut their affair among themselves and become separate pieces, each piece has its own method and law, each piece has its own obligations and its own banner, as if their gods were many. Will they be left in this state, or will they return to Us in the end?

﴿To Us they will all return.﴾ (21:93): So, you are one community in creation from the beginning, and one community in the return and in the end. Why, then, do you differ in the middle of the road?

Thus, disagreement arises from the difference of method, whereas the one who laid down the method ought to be one. The Prophet (ﷺ) came as the seal of the messages, and his law came comprehensive of the merits of the previous laws, indeed surpassing them with the merits that the ages following his mission require.

So it was required that the believing community gather upon that comprehensive, all-encompassing, complete method, which cannot be surpassed, and thereby the unity of the community would be realized, and its obligations would proceed from one God, so that there would be no room in it for desires, nor for temporal authorities, nor for base aims.

Therefore, if the groups that claim to be Islam multiply and scatter, we say to them: be one group; otherwise, which of your groups is in the right? For God Most High addressed His Prophet (ﷺ) saying: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects — you are not [associated] with them in anything.﴾ (6:159)

Those who call to one call do not scatter except by following desires and aims; but the true religion is the one that comes in accordance with the desire of heaven, agreeing with what God Most High has approved for His creation.

The believers have turned away from the gathering point that unites them by God's command, so the unity has dispersed from them, and they have turned their backs on one another, until nothing unites them except the saying "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God." As for their methods and laws, they have taken them from here and there, and these laws will bite them, and these civilizations will fail them, and they will see their evil effects; then they will return in the end to Islam, for it is their sole refuge, just as we now hear the cry: there is no solution but Islam.

Yes, Islam is the solution to problems, crises, disputes and leaderships; a solution to the pluralism that has weakened the Muslims and undermined their brotherhood, of which God said: ﴿And hold firmly to the rope of God, all together, and do not become divided. And remember the favor of God upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and you became, by His favor, brothers.﴾ (3:103)

By God, if we returned to the one rope of God and held fast to it, and desires did not play with us, we would return to the one community that ruled the whole world.

So: ﴿To Us they will all return.﴾ (21:93): that is, in the Hereafter, for reckoning. And I say: O Lord, perhaps this return will be in this world, in that the laws of men bite us, so we flee to God and return to Him anew, and our glory returns to us, and the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ) comes true concerning us: "Islam began as a stranger and will return as it began, a stranger, so blessed are the strangers."(1)

This understanding is reinforced and this hope strengthened by the saying of God Most High after it:

﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed We are recording it for him.﴾ (21:94)

(1) Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (145), Kitab al-Iman, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (3986), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).

Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, resumes with us the exhortation through righteous action, to give us hope if we return to God. The whole world bears witness that any false principle, or deceptive slogan that men use to adorn their desires, does not endure long but collapses, even after a time, and its adherents come to see that it was an error and turn away from it.

An example of this is the communist ideology that prevailed in Russia since 1917, in whose name sanctities were violated, blood was shed, homes were demolished, and wealth was seized. Having once been a nation that exported food to the countries of the world, it now begs from the countries of the world. Yet they were the first to cry out against this ideology and to suffer from these laws.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer...﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:94], it links righteous action to faith (iman), because faith is the starting point of the believer in everything he does and everything he refrains from, so that by his deeds he may attain the happiness of this world and the happiness of the Hereafter.

As for one who does good for its own sake and out of humanity and chivalry, and yet all of this is ultimately not free of desires and aims, he shall take his share in this world, and he will be honored, lordly, and renowned therein, but he has no share in the reward of the Hereafter, because he did good while God was not in his mind.

Almighty God gives us an example of this in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert plain, which the thirsty one takes for water, until when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full...﴾ [al-Nur 24:39]

That is: he is surprised by the existence of a God who calls him to account and recompenses him, a matter that had not been on his mind. Then it is said to him: "You acted to be seen, and you have been seen," and the matter is ended. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase him in his tilth...﴾ [al-Shura 42:20]: that is, We give him his reward in another world that has no end. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura 42:20].

Because he worked for people, let him take his reward from them: they will immortalize his memory and set up exhibitions and statues for him, and so on.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So there is no denial of his striving...﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:94]: that is, We will not diminish his due nor ever deny his striving. ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:94]: We record his deeds and preserve them. It is supposed that a person is the one who records for himself; but if your Lord records your deed for you, the one by which He rewards you, and records it upon Himself, then there is no doubt that it is a precise record that does not diminish for you the weight of an atom of your deed.

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they should not return.﴾ (21:95)

﴿Forbidden...﴾ (21:95): i.e., impossible, it is not permissible that it should be. "A town": any town which We have destroyed, because it denied the messengers and took towards them a stance of obstinate opposition, contention and resistance, so God destroyed it for its sins in this world. Is it conceivable, after this, that We would leave it in the Hereafter without taking it to account for its sins?

Therefore, it is necessary that it return to Us in the Hereafter, so that We may hold it to account with the everlasting, eternal reckoning, and not be satisfied with the reckoning of this world, which comes to an end.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 96:

Then the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) says:

﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm down from every mound.﴾ (96):

The story of Gog and Magog (Ya'juj wa Ma'juj) appears at the end of Surat al-Kahf, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the wandering man who traversed the earth, and the revelation came: ﴿They ask you about Dhu'l-Qarnayn. Say: I shall recite to you a remembrance of him.﴾ (83) [al-Kahf].

The scholars have spoken about Dhu'l-Qarnayn. Some said he is Cyrus (Qurush), and some said he is Alexander the Great (al-Iskandar al-Akbar). The Qur'an does not concern itself with the person; otherwise it would have mentioned him by name. The Qur'an does not date him, nor does it erect a statue for him. Rather, it intends to focus on the attributes that concern the Truth and concern creation.

It is sufficient for us to know that he is a human being whom God established on the earth. That is, He gave him the causes of strength, the causes of awe and dominion, and all the foundations of power: He gave him wealth, knowledge and armies. Yet he was not content with all of that, but ﴿followed a course﴾ (85) [al-Kahf]: that is, he took the means that lead to good.

We have previously spoken about the personification of the hero in the Qur'anic stories, because the Qur'an does not write the history of the individual, nor does it give him particularity. Rather, it wants him general, so that he becomes an example to be emulated, through which lessons are drawn and the intended effect of the story is produced.

What concerns us in the story of Dhu'l-Qarnayn is that he is a man who was established in the earth, and his attributes were such-and-such. What concerns us about the People of the Cave is that they were youths who believed in their Lord, held fast to their religion and creed, and sacrificed for its sake. The persons, the time, the place and the number do not matter to us.

Therefore, the Qur'an left all these matters unspecified: whatever youths, in whatever time, in whatever place, and under whatever names, could take this stance of faith. Had we identified and named them, people would have said: this is an incident specific to those people, or that they are examples that do not recur. Therefore the Qur'an left them unspecified, so that they would be a lesson and a model that travels through all time.

Likewise, when the Qur'an wished to set forth a parable for those who disbelieved, it mentioned the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot without naming them; and similarly it set forth a parable for those who believed in the wife of Pharaoh and did not say who she was (2). The purpose of setting forth these parables is not the persons; rather, it is to make us know that a woman has the freedom of belief and independence of opinion, so she is not a follower of anyone, as evidenced by the fact that Noah and Lot could not each guide his wife.

And Pharaoh, the disbeliever who claimed divinity, could not prevent his wife from believing, and she is the one who said: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and deliver me from the wrongdoing people.﴾ (11) [al-Tahrim].

So what concerns us in the story of "Dhu'l-Qarnayn" is that God established him in the earth and gave him every cause of strength and dominion; therefore He entrusted him to be a balance of good and truth, and delegated to him to judge among creation by what he sees as truth and justice.

﴿Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and he found near it a people. We said: O Dhu'l-Qarnayn, either you punish them, or you adopt good treatment toward them.﴾ (86) [al-Kahf].

Because We had established him and entrusted him, he used the establishment in its place and took the trust with its due right, and said: ﴿As for him who does wrong, we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment.﴾ (87) [al-Kahf]: that is, we punish him according to the measure of our capacity, then he is returned to his Lord, Who punishes him according to the measure of His capacity, may He be exalted.

﴿And as for him who believes and does righteous deeds, he will have a fine reward, and we will speak to him of our command with ease.﴾ (88) [al-Kahf]

Thus is the constitution of life from the ruler empowered over creation: the constitution of reward and punishment by which the affairs of the lands and their people are set right. When he sees a shortcoming, he must take the hand of its doer, whatever his station, fearing no one, flattering no one, and not fearing the blame of any blamer concerning God. And if he sees the good and diligent person, he rewards him and recompenses him.

We see this law in our society nearly suspended among those who work, so that the wheat is mixed with the chaff, affairs deteriorate, and other measures of reward and punishment have entered among us, for which God has sent down no authority. The balances have been overturned, so that the idle boast and the diligent good-doers are discouraged.

﴿Until, when he reached the rising-place of the sun, he found it rising upon a people for whom We had made no shelter against it.﴾ (90) [al-Kahf]:

This is all that God has told us. It appears that in his general wandering he reached lands where the sun remains shining for three or six months without setting, so he found for them no shelter from the sun that would screen them from it, any darkness. ﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers, he found beside them a people who scarcely understood speech.﴾ (93) [al-Kahf]

Nevertheless, he strove to make himself understood by them and to address them, out of his eagerness for their benefit and for what would set them right. This is the attribute of the believing ruler when he is established in the earth, given the means of leadership, and delegated over God's creation. Had he not been eager for their benefit, he would have found an excuse in that he could not understand them and they could not understand him.

When they arrived at a common language, perhaps the language of sign by which we communicate with, for example, a mute person:

﴿They said: O Dhu'l-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the earth. So shall we pay you a tribute (kharj) (3) on condition that you make between us and them a barrier?﴾ (94) [al-Kahf].

Then he commanded them to bring pieces of iron, and he kindled fire upon them until they glowed red, and said: ﴿Bring me, that I may pour molten copper over it.﴾ (96) [al-Kahf]: Thus he made for them the barrier that protects them from these people. His benefit to them was not confined to this particular matter itself; rather, he benefited them with a benefit that gives them good and strength so that they would not be exposed to its like afterward, acting upon the wisdom that says: Do not give me a fish, but teach me how to fish.

This is because he made them partners in the work, so that they would feel its importance and hold firmly to preserving and maintaining it, and when they are exposed to such a situation again they do not wait for someone to build for them.

This is the model that the story of "Dhu'l-Qarnayn" presents, and it is a model suitable for every age, every place, and every ruler whom God has established in the earth and into whose hands He has placed the crisis of affairs. In a hadith about the best deed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Help a craftsman, or have a craft made for a clumsy man" (4).

The sayings have differed concerning: who are Gog and Magog? Some say they are the Tatars. Another says: the Mongols. Another says: they are the Hitit, or the Sardiyal, or the tribes of the Huns.

If identifying them had any benefit, the Qur'an would have named them. What matters from their story is that they are a people who corrupt the earth and do not leave the righteous in their righteousness. When the one established in the earth confronts them, he must stand between them and this corruption directed at others. As for us, we must not corrupt the righteous as they do, but leave the righteous in their righteousness, and indeed increase them in righteousness.

In Dhu'l-Qarnayn's building of the barrier there are lessons that those in authority who bear the affairs of creation must heed. Among these lessons: he did not stop at their request to build a barrier that would prevent the harm of their enemy; rather, he strove and raised the matter to what was better for them. A solid barrier, firm as a single piece, is easy to demolish or to pass through; therefore he said: ﴿Help me with strength, and I will make between you and them a rampart.﴾ (95) [al-Kahf]

They asked for a barrier (sadd), while he said: a rampart (radm). He raised the idea for them and wished to build for them a barrier of a special form that absorbs shocks and does not affect its structure, for he placed between the two sides a rampart, as if it were a zipper giving the barrier a kind of flexibility. Thus must the believer be when bearing the responsibility for creation.

When they offered him money in return for his work, he refused and said: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength...﴾ (95) [al-Kahf]: that is, I have abundant wealth from God's bounty, but help me with the strength you have. So: the alms of strength is that it prevents corruption by others.

Let us return to His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose...﴾ (96) [al-Anbiya'], which is connected to His saying: ﴿And they have divided their affair among themselves...﴾ (93) [al-Anbiya']. The dispersal and division of the people of good opens the way for the people of corruption against them, and the least they say about them is that, had they been upon good, they would have benefited themselves. So leave their talk aside. Thus the people of falsehood weaken the arm of the people of truth and turn people away from them.

﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose...﴾ (96) [al-Anbiya']: that is, the elements of corruption and sedition have come into existence in the cosmos, and the elements of corruption and sedition cannot establish themselves, nor find the opportunity and temporal authority, except when the people of truth are heedless and scattered, so that they do not repel them, nor take their hands.

Gog and Magog are the people of corruption in every age and place. Genghis Khan (Jinkizkhan) destroyed the first Islamic state in Khwarazm, whose ruler was Qutb Arsalan. Then from his third line of descendants came Hulagu, who entered Baghdad, the seat of the Islamic caliphate, devastated it, killed its people until the blood flowed, and threw the Islamic books into the river until they became a bridge over which they crossed. These are the ones we call the Tatars.

So: the Qur'an related to us from ancient history the story of Gog and Magog in the days of Dhu'l-Qarnayn, and then we saw them in our Islamic life. God willed that the Muslims benefit from the attacks of these barbarians, and that their provinces unite and repel the Tatar attacks on the land of Egypt under the leadership of Qutuz and al-Zahir Baybars, two examples of those established in the earth, although they were Mamluks.

These Tatar attacks by the corruptors in the earth were savage, barbaric assaults. And the descendants of those Gog and Magog of the modern age have gathered in civilizational assaults that invade us with their civilization: they are the Crusaders, who were defeated before the unity of the Muslims under the leadership of Salah al-Din.

Thus, throughout history, we are victorious when we are one nation, and we are defeated when we scatter and split into nations and factions. These are facts that confirm the truth of the Qur'an in what it directed us to: unity and not dividing.

Then He, exalted be He, says: ﴿And they will swarm down from every mound.﴾ (96) [al-Anbiya']:

al-Hadab: the raised place. We say: so-and-so is hunch-backed, meaning there is a raised area on his back. Likewise these corruptors came from raised places on the plateau of northern China. The meaning of ﴿yansilun﴾ (96) [al-Anbiya']: that is, they hasten. From it we say: "insalla al-qumash" (the cloth unravelled), because cloth is composed of warp (sada) and weft (luhma), meaning longitudinal threads and transverse threads, which interlace to form the cloth. The unravelling of cloth is that the transverse threads are pulled out and their interlacing with the longitudinal threads is undone, while the longitudinal threads are not pulled out, because they are always held firm by the bending of the warp over the weft.

1 al-Hadab: what is raised of the earth. That is, they come from every side, and even if it is high and difficult, nothing hinders them, because on level ground they are swifter and movement is easier for them; so they come from every direction even if it is split. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/144].
2 God the Exalted says: ﴿God sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot; they were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, and they availed them nothing against God...(10)﴾ [al-Tahrim].
3 Kharj and kharaj: what the owner of wealth gives the worker employed by him as wages for his work, or what he pays of zakat to the imam. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/190].
4 From Abu Dhar, may God be pleased with him, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, which deeds are best? He said: Belief in God and striving in His way. I said: Which slaves are best? He said: The most precious of them to their people and the most costly. I said: And if I do not do that? He said: "Help a craftsman, or have a craft made for a clumsy man." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (84), Book of Faith, and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2518) with the wording: "Help a dispossessed (ḍā'i'an) man."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 21, verse 97:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly. "Woe to us! We were heedless of this; nay, we were wrongdoers."﴾

So the people of corruption come rushing from every hill and direction, but their corruption will not last long, for the Resurrection has drawn near. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split﴾ [al-Qamar]. And He says: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it…﴾ [al-Nahl]. This is an alert to the heedless, a warning to the transgressing people of corruption, and an assurance and hope for the oppressed and weakened who have been wronged: be at ease, for the time of recompense has drawn near.

﴿The true promise has drawn near…﴾ [al-Anbiya']. The "true promise" means the truthful one, which its giver has the power to carry out. For one may make a promise yet not have the power to fulfil it; that is a promise, but a false one. Promises differ according to the nobility of the one who promises, his capabilities, and his ability to carry out what he has promised.

But however many capabilities you have, and however many means of execution you possess, can you guarantee that circumstances and conditions will enable you to carry it out? All of this is possessed only by Allah, mighty and majestic. When He promises, He fulfils what He has promised. So the true promise, then, is the promise of Allah.

When the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the true promise draws near…﴾ [al-Anbiya'], then take heed, and do not measure the world by its basic lifespan; rather, measure the world by your own lifespan in it. This is the world as far as you are concerned, and the worlds of others are no concern of yours. If you do not know when you will part from your world, there is no doubt that your life is near, and the true promise has drawn near for you.

Likewise, the length of your stay in your grave until the Hour is established will pass over you like an hour of a day, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿As though they had not remained but an hour of the day…﴾ [Yunus, 45].

If each of us were alert to the concealment of the time of his own death by Allah, he would know that in this concealment lies the greatest clarity. For when He concealed it, we watch for it in every blink of an eye and every breath. Therefore they say: "Whoever dies, his resurrection has come" [a saying of the Prophet], because the Resurrection means reckoning and recompense for deeds, and whoever dies, his deeds are cut off and his record is folded up.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly…﴾ [al-Anbiya', 97]:

The promise of Allah here is the Resurrection, and it surprises us and comes upon us suddenly. Therefore we say that in "fa-idhā" (then, behold) it is the sudden-surprise particle, as you say: "I went out and behold, a lion at the door," meaning: I was surprised by it. Likewise, at the hour the Hour arises, it will surprise everyone, and no one knows what to do.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly…﴾ [al-Anbiya', 97]. The staring of the eye comes when you see something you did not expect and did not take into account; you look astonished, your upper eyelid freezes as it normally moves over the eye, and you cannot even blink or flutter your eyelids.

In another verse He, exalted is He, says: ﴿He only defers them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ [Ibrahim, 42].

If you wish to see the staring of the eye, look at a person who is surprised by something that was not in his mind: without any awareness, by his natural instinct, you will see his eyes fixed, his eyelid not coming down.

Then they say: ﴿"Woe to us! We were heedless of this…"﴾ [al-Anbiya', 97]:

The situation is not limited to the staring of the eyes; the instruments of perception also move. The tongue says: "Woe to us!" This is a call to woe, meaning: your time has come, and nothing remains for them but to say: "O torment, this is your time, so be present."

Woe (wayl) is swift destruction, which they call upon. Does a person seek destruction and invoke it for himself? We say: yes, when a person commits an act and finds its evil consequences, and the bitter reality confronts him, he inclines to torment himself. Do you not hear such people say: "I deserve it… I deserve the beating…"? It is self-blame and self-reproach for what it did, for it is the one that brought him into this predicament.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf, 67].

So why would he not reproach his self and ask for punishment for it, when it was the one that cast him into ruin? In this situation their standards which they were accustomed to in the world are overturned: the friends in evil and in sin are now the enemies.

﴿"We were heedless of this…"﴾ [al-Anbiya', 97]: this situation was not in our minds, and we did not take it into account. Heedlessness (ghafla) is to push away from your mind what ought to be always in your mind.

But what heedlessness is this, by Allah, when Allah, mighty and majestic, reminds us of this situation at every time of night or day? Do you not see that He, glory be to Him, named the Qur'an "a reminder" (dhikr) in order to remove this heedlessness from us? Whenever you are heedless, it reminds you, stirs your feelings, and arouses your emotions.

So the matter is not heedlessness; therefore we see them correcting their own words, saying: ﴿"Nay, we were wrongdoers"﴾ [al-Anbiya', 97], because they remembered that Allah, exalted is He, had often stirred their emotions and moved their feelings towards faith, yet they did not respond.

Therefore they admit their wrongdoing here, and they cannot deny it in such a situation. Lying is no longer useful; perhaps they hope by this truthfulness to obtain some mercy, and think that truthfulness will benefit them. But far-fetched is that.

It is as though the Truthful One, glory be to Him, relates this confrontation of theirs when the Resurrection surprises them with its terrors, their eyes stare fixedly at it, and some of them say: ﴿"Woe to us! We were heedless of this…"﴾ [al-Anbiya', 97]. Then their brethren answer them: What heedlessness is this, when Allah has been reminding us of the Resurrection and of this situation at every time: ﴿"Nay, we were wrongdoers"﴾ [al-Anbiya', 97].

"Bal" (nay, rather) is a particle of retraction from the preceding speech and of affirmation of the following speech. Thus they review themselves, and some of them confront others, but after it is too late.

[Footnote 1] "Shakhasa basaruhu": his eyes opened and did not blink, from fear, terror and bewilderment; it is a metaphor for the intensity of the terror and dread on the Day of Resurrection. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/343].

[Footnote 2] Mentioned by al-'Ajluni in Kashf al-Khafa' (hadith no. 2618) from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, and its completion is: "Increase your remembrance of death, for if you remember it in prosperity it will sour it for you, and if you remember it in hardship it will widen it for you. Death is the Resurrection."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 21, verse 98:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to it [destined to] come.﴾ (98)

Those whom you took as gods besides Allah, of idols, images, the sun, the moon and trees, will go ahead of you into Hell, so as to cut off from you every hope of salvation. For when they see the punishment, they may remember these [gods], think of seeking refuge in them and calling on them for help, in the hope that they will bring them out of this predicament. Indeed, they had said about them earlier: ﴿These are our intercessors with Allah…﴾ (18) [Yunus].

And they said: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in closeness.﴾ (3) [al-Zumar].

Therefore, Allah gathers them all together in Hell, to cut off their hopes, and the shame of the worshipped and the disappointment of the worshipper become manifest, for he comes to the Fire and finds that his deity has gone ahead of him to it. But is this statement absolute? The disbelievers worshipped idols, and among them were those who worshipped ʿIsa (peace be upon him), those who worshipped ʿUzayr, and those who worshipped the angels. Will these, too, be gathered with their worshippers in the Fire?

If we take this view, their entry into the Fire is like the entry of Ibrahim [into the fire], for Allah gathered for him the Fire and safety at the same time; their presence will be merely so that their worshippers may see them and know that they do not benefit them.(2)

The meaning of ﴿ḥaṣab jahannam⟩ (98) [al-Anbiya’]: ḥaṣab (fuel) is like ḥaṭab (firewood), and it is everything with which the fire is kindled, whether wood, straw, petroleum or electricity. In another verse: ﴿Its fuel is men and stones…﴾ (6) [al-Tahrim]. Therefore the Fire itself yearns for the disbelievers, awaits them and longs for them, as the Exalted says: ﴿On the Day when We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ (30) [Qaf].

And the Exalted says: ﴿When they are cast into it, they hear from it a roaring while it boils, almost bursting with rage…﴾ (7–8) [al-Mulk].

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿You are to it [destined to] come﴾ (98) [al-Anbiya’]: wurud here means entering and direct contact, not like the wurud in the other verse: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it…﴾ (71) [Maryam].

(1) This word is read in three ways in the Qur'an:
1. ḥaṣab jahannam: the reading of the majority.
2. ḥaṭab jahannam: the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and ʿAʾisha.
3. ḥaḍab jahannam: the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4524]

(2) From Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: When there was revealed ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to it [destined to] come﴾ (98) [al-Anbiya’], Ibn al-Zaba'ra said: Do you not claim, O Muhammad, that ʿIsa is a righteous servant, that ʿUzayr is a righteous servant, and that the angels are righteous? He said: Yes. He said: Then these Christians worship ʿIsa, these Jews worship ʿUzayr, and these Banu Mulayh worship the angels. The people of Makkah raised an outcry and rejoiced, and then there was revealed ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us – those will be kept far away from it﴾ (101) [al-Anbiya’], [referring to] ʿUzayr, ʿIsa and the angels. Abu Dawud recorded it in his Nasikh, and Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Tabarani [also did]; al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/679).

(3) The scholars differed about the meaning of wurud in His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it…﴾ (71) [Maryam], with several views, among them:
- Wurud means entering; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Khalid ibn Maʿdan, Ibn Jurayj and others.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿If these were gods, they would not have entered it. And all of them will abide therein.﴾

Because they will enter and find their gods before them, so that their hope in the intercession they imagine will be cut off, just as He, the Exalted, said concerning Pharaoh: ﴿He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire...﴾ [Hud]. Their leader and their chief goes ahead of them and precedes them into the Fire. Had he not been before them, they would have thought that he would rescue them from this predicament. And if these were gods, as you claim, they would not have entered the Fire.

As for the meaning of ﴿And all of them will abide therein﴾ [al-Anbiya]: the known characteristic of fire is that it consumes what is in it and then comes to an end, but this Fire has no end. Whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, and thus the Fire remains blazing and never goes out. As for the meaning of ﴿all﴾ [al-Anbiya]: it refers to both the worshipper and the worshipped.

The Zafir (the exhaled breath, the sound of groaning) is known to be what comes out of the process of breathing. A person takes in oxygen when inhaling and releases carbon dioxide when exhaling. We notice here that the expression is limited to the zafir without the shahiq (inhalation), because the zafir is the hot air that comes out, and there is no air in the Fire for inhalation. It is as if they have no inhalation at all. May Allah protect us from the punishment.

﴿وهم فيها لا يسمعون﴾ [al-Anbiya]: "And they therein will not hear" (21:100).

This is one of the verses at which the orientalists have paused, because there are other verses that establish for them in the Fire both hearing and speech, as in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿ونادى أصحاب الجنة أصحاب النار أن قد وجدنا ما وعدنا ربنا حقا فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقا قالوا نعم فأذن مؤذن بينهم أن لعنة الله على الظالمين﴾ [al-A'raf]: "And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, 'We have found what our Lord promised us to be true; have you found what your Lord promised to be true?' They will say, 'Yes.' Then a announcer will announce between them: 'The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers'" (7:44).

Yes, they do hear, but they do not hear words that delight; rather they hear rebuke and reproach, as in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿ونادى أصحاب النار أصحاب الجنة أن أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله قالوا إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين﴾ [al-A'raf]: "And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: 'Pour upon us some water or from what Allah has provided you.' They will say, 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers.'" (7:50)

Following the mention of the recompense of the disbelievers in the Fire, He (glory be to Him) mentioned the opposite, and mentioning the opposite clarifies the meaning. Consider His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾ [Al-Infitar].

And He says: ﴿So let them laugh a little and weep much...﴾ [At-Tawbah: 82]. Therefore, the comparison remains vivid in the mind.

As for the meaning of ﴿those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us...﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 101]: al-Husna (الحسنى) is the feminine of al-ahsan (الأحسن, "the best"). You say: "This is hasan (حسن, good) and this is hasanah (حسنة, good)"; if you want emphasis you say: "This is ahsan (أحسن, best), and this is husna (حسنى, best)," like akbar (أكبر, greater) and kubra (كبرى, greatest). The meaning of ﴿those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us...﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 101] is that they are among the people of obedience and among the people of Paradise; thus God's judgment for them is established. God, exalted is He, took a portion of His creation and said: "These are for Paradise and I do not care, and these are for the Fire and I do not care" (1).

Do not say: "What is the sin of these?" Because He, glory be to Him, judged by His foreknowledge of the obedience of these and the disobedience of those.

As for His saying: ﴿Those will be kept far from it [the Fire]﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 101], meaning: they will be kept far away from the Fire.

(1) From Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When Allah created Adam, He struck his right shoulder and brought forth a white offspring as if they were ants, and struck his left shoulder and brought forth a black offspring as if they were coals. Then He said to the one in His right hand: 'To Paradise, and I do not care.' And He said to the one in His left hand: 'To the Fire, and I do not care.'" Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (6/441).

(2) Ibn 'Abbas said: "Those are the friends of Allah; they pass over the Sirat swiftly, faster than lightning, while the disbelievers remain in it, kneeling." Others said: "Rather, it was revealed as an exception from those worshipped, and 'Uzayr and al-Masih were excluded," as narrated by Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war from Ibn Jurayj and Uthman ibn 'Ata' from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/198).

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿They will not hear its faint sound, and they will abide forever in what their souls desire.﴾

*Hasis* (the faint sound) of the Fire: its roaring and the sounds that issue from it at the very beginning of its blazing. ﴿And they will abide forever in what their souls desire﴾ [al-Anbiya]. He did not say "and they will abide forever with what their souls desire," but rather ﴿in what their souls desire...﴾ [al-Anbiya]. It is as if they are immersed in bliss through what their souls desire, as if the desires of their souls were a vessel that contains them and envelops them. This stirs the longing of the people of goodness and righteousness for Paradise and its bliss, so that we may work for it and prepare for this bliss.

We have said before that a person toils at the beginning of his life, learns a trade, or obtains a certificate so that he may benefit from it later and find rest in the future of his life. Your comfort is in proportion to your toil and effort, for every fruit must have tilling and exertion, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not waste the reward of one who does good work.

We used to see some farmers spend their day in their fields, with unkempt clothes and a shabby appearance, occupied with nothing but working on their crops. And you would see another, neatly dressed and clean, sitting in the café, happy with this ease, and perhaps mocking his companion who wears himself out at work. Yet when the time of harvest comes, the worker finds the fruit of his labor, while the lazy one finds nothing but regret and remorse.

So your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has given you strength and limbs, and He wants you to move, and in movement there is blessing. If a farmer sat turning over his land and stirring its soil without planting it, Allah would still compensate him, and his toil would bear fruit, even if he found something in the earth that he could benefit from, such as a gold ring or other things.

A person's luxury and comfort are in proportion to his toil at the beginning of his life. The one who toils and sweats, for example, for ten years will rest for the rest of his life; if he toils for twenty years, he rests, and his children rest after him; if he toils for thirty years, his grandchildren rest, and so on.

The luxury of the learned depends on his certificate: this one has an intermediate certificate, that one has an advanced one, and this one has obtained a doctorate, so that he may have a position and standing in his society.

But however much a person prepares for himself the delights and luxuries of this life, it remains a bliss in proportion to his capabilities and energies. For this reason, we mentioned that when we traveled to San Francisco we saw one of the luxurious hotels, and they said that King Faisal, may Allah have mercy on him, used to stay there. So we wished to tour it, and indeed we took in its manifestations of luxury and grandeur and the splendor of its architecture. Some people of high standing were with me, and I said to them: "This is what the servants have prepared for the servants, so what of what the Lord of the servants has prepared for the servants?"

So when you see the people of bliss and luxury in this world, do not resent them, for their bliss reminds you of and makes you long for the bliss of the Hereafter.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿The Great Terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them: "This is your Day, which you were promised."﴾

That is because they are in lasting bliss that does not end, and a gift that is not cut off. Poverty will not overtake you in it, nor will death overtake it. Therefore, ﴿The Great Terror will not grieve them...﴾ [al-Anbiya']: for what terror is there with this enduring blessing? Or: the terror of the Resurrection and its horrors will not grieve them.

And His saying: ﴿And the angels will receive them: "This is your Day, which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya']: God has indeed fulfilled His promise to you, and has accomplished for you what He promised you of the bliss of the Hereafter.

(1) Mujahid said: "The angels who were their companions in the world will receive them on the Day of Resurrection, and they will say: 'We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter; we will not leave you until you enter Paradise.'" Recorded by Ibn Abi Hatim, and mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/683).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 104:

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿On the Day We shall roll up the heaven like the rolling up of the written scroll. As We began the first creation, so We shall bring it back; a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever the Doer.﴾

That is: what befalls the disbelievers of punishment and what befalls the believers of bliss will occur ﴿on the Day We shall roll up the heaven like the rolling up of the written scroll﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:104]. The word "Day" (yawm) denotes a time and a container for events. So what befalls the disbelievers of torment and humiliation, and what befalls the believers of eternal bliss, will all take place on this Day.

The "sijil" (scroll) is the parchment, and the paper on which one writes is called a sijil. This is why people say, "We record (nusajjil) such-and-such," meaning we write it on a sheet so that it is preserved. The "kitab" (book) is that which is written.

The Truthful, glory be to Him, says in another verse: ﴿And the heavens will be folded up in His right hand...﴾ [al-Zumar 39:67]. He folds them by His power, for the right hand among us is the one that acts upon things. But we do not take the folding to be the folding we know; rather we take it within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ [al-Shura 42:11].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As We began the first creation, so We shall bring it back﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:104] indicates to us that the Truthful, glory be to Him, is speaking of the first creation, and ﴿We shall bring it back﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:104] indicates the existence of a second creation.

Thus His saying, exalted is He, in another place: ﴿On the Day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ibrahim 14:48] is evidence that the first creation was a creation in which there are causes and there is the one who causes. The Truthful, glory be to Him, gave you in this world the means of life: the sun, the moon, the rain, the earth, the water... etc., and these are matters in which you have no part. All that is required of you is to use the mind which Allah created to advance with these things and to enjoy them.

As for the second creation, you merely receive bliss from Allah without taking the causes that you know in this world, because the Hereafter does not stand upon causes but upon the One who causes, glory be to Him. When you see in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, you know that your Lord's action for you is greater than your action for yourself.

However far the causes of luxury in this world advance, and however much creatures devise means of comfort and refined service, the most they have is that you press a button that opens the door for you, or brings you food or coffee. But I challenge the world, with all its progress and technology, to provide me with whatever food or drink comes to my mind, so that I see it before me without speaking, for this matter is possible only for Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic.

So His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, so We shall bring it back﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:104] means not merely that He restores it as it was, but that We bring it back better and more excellent than it was, such that the bliss reaches you to the point that a thing comes to your mind and you find it before you. Indeed, the believer in Paradise takes a kind of fruit and says, "We have eaten the like of this before," and it is said to him: "It is not so; rather it is better than what you have eaten, and more wholesome than what you have tasted." If you were to take, for example, an apple of this world, you would find it subject to the type of soil, the water, the surrounding atmosphere, and the pesticides on which crops nowadays cannot do without... etc. But the apple of the Hereafter is something entirely different; it is a divine craftsmanship and a Lordly preparation.

It is as if the Truthful, glory be to Him, draws the attention of His servants to the fact that His care for them is better than their care for themselves, because He, glory be to Him, is more entitled to us than we are to ourselves, and so that we may know the difference between a thing in our hands and a thing in His hand, glory be to Him.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever the Doer﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:104]: that is, nothing takes us out of what We have promised, and no one opposes Us.

Footnote 1: Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (5/3721): "It was narrated with a marfu' chain from the hadith of Abu Hurayra that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The earth will be changed to other than the earth; it will be spread out and stretched like a tanned leather of 'Ukaz, you will see no crookedness or elevation in it. Then Allah will drive the creation with one driving, and they will be in the second [state] in the same places as in the first: whoever was in its belly will be in its belly, and whoever was on its surface will be on its surface.'" Mentioned by al-Ghaznawi.

Footnote 2: This is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in likeness﴾ [al-Baqara 2:25].

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We had written in the Psalms (al-Zabur)(1) after the Reminder (al-dhikr) that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ (21:105)

Writing (al-kutub) means recording. But the knowledge of Allah is eternal and needs no recording; recording is for our sake, so that we may be reassured. It is like when you take a loan from your companion and there is trust between you, and you feel secure in one another, yet still you write down the loan and record it so that the soul may be at rest.

As for the meaning of ﴿We had written in the Psalms﴾ (21:105): al-Zabur is the Book that was sent down to the Prophet of Allah, Dawud (David). The meaning of al-Zabur is "that which is written." If it is taken in its general sense, it applies to every Book that Allah has sent down.

As for ﴿after the Reminder﴾ (21:105): al-dhikr is used sometimes for the Qur'an and sometimes for the earlier Books. Since al-Zabur is applied to every Book that Allah has sent down, al-dhikr must have a broader meaning. Therefore al-dhikr is applied to the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), because it is the record of the record, and everything is in it.

So the meaning of ﴿We had written in the Psalms﴾ (21:105) is: in the Books that were sent down to the Prophets, We wrote what We had written in the Preserved Tablet, or what We had written in the Psalms. It does not mean that Prophet Dawud was given more than what the others were given.

As for ﴿after the Reminder﴾ (21:105): this indicates that one thing is prior to another. We say: the Qur'an is the ancient Speech of Allah, and there is no scripture older than it. What is meant here by ﴿after the Reminder﴾ (21:105) is a sequence of mention, not a sequence of time.

So what did Allah write for Dawud in the Psalms? He wrote for him ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ (21:105). The word "earth" (al-ard), when used in its general sense, is intended to mean the whole terrestrial globe.

It may be restricted by a specific description, as in ﴿the Holy Land﴾ (5:21).

And in ﴿I will not leave the land﴾ (12:80): that is, the land in which he was.

Here, the Exalted says ﴿that the earth...﴾ (21:105): that is, the earth in general. ﴿shall inherit it﴾ (21:105): that is, it will be a formal right for the righteous servants of Allah. Which earth is this? Is it the earth we are upon now, or the changed earth?

Since we are speaking of the beginning of creation and its return, the intended meaning is the changed earth that will be restored in the Hereafter (2), which the righteous servants of Allah will inherit. The inheritance here is as in His saying: ﴿That is the Garden which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do﴾ (7:43).

So who inherits this earth?

When Allah, the Exalted, created creation, He prepared the Garden to accommodate all of the children of Adam if they believe, and He prepared the Fire to accommodate all of the children of Adam if they disbelieve. So there is no crowding in the matter in any case. When the people of the Garden enter the Garden and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, the places of the people of the Fire in the Garden remain empty; so Allah bequeaths them to the people of the Garden, divides them among them, and widens for them the places from which the people of disbelief were barred.

Or we may say: the earth is intended to mean the earth of this world (3). The meaning would then be that Allah empowers the righteous from among the earth, the righteous one who cultivates it even if he is a disbeliever, because Allah, the Exalted, does not deprive a person of the fruits of his deeds, even if he is a disbeliever. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ (42:20).

However, the cultivation of the earth by disbelievers and their building of civilization soon brings calamities upon them, and their civilization turns against them. Here we see the calamities of advanced and developed nations and the incurable social diseases they suffer from. Thus the cultivation of the earth is not merely economy, food, drink and luxury. In Sweden, for example, which is among the highest countries in the world in income, there is nevertheless the highest rate of suicide and the highest rate of deviance, and this is the "narrow life" (al-ma'ishah al-dank) of which the Noble Qur'an speaks in His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed, for him is a narrow life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ (20:124).

So constriction (al-dank) does not mean only poverty and need; it has many other forms.

Therefore: do not measure the level of civilization by material things alone; take into account all the other aspects. Whoever perfects the worldly material aspects takes them and luxuriates in them in this world, while religious, moral and ethical righteousness is the path to the luxury of this world and the bliss of the Hereafter.

Thus the verse ﴿My righteous servants shall inherit it﴾ (21:105) includes both worldly material righteousness and the spiritual righteousness of the Hereafter. If you take righteousness absolutely, without faith, you will find its fruit for a time, then it will turn against you. Where are the people of the ancient civilizations, such as 'Ad, Thamud and the Pharaohs?

All these civilizations, with all they attained, could not preserve permanence for themselves; they passed away and perished.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [the people of] Iram of the pillars, the like of which had not been produced in the land? And Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley? And Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?﴾ (89:6–10).

They were refined civilizations, buried under layers of dust; we do not even know their places. But if you take the spiritual righteousness, the methodical righteousness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, you will gain both this world and the Hereafter. This is because the movement of life needs a method to regulate it: do this and do not do that. This is not something humans can accomplish; but the Lord of humans is the One who knows what benefits them and legislates for them what makes them happy.

The method of Allah alone is what commands us and forbids us, and informs us of the lawful and the unlawful. It is for us to implement it, and it is for the rulers and the holders of authority, who hold the scale of justice, to oversee this implementation, appointing whoever is fit for the task and who performs it in the best manner. Otherwise the condition of society will be corrupted. The ruler supervises and monitors, encourages the worker and punishes the idle, and places the right man in the right place.

Thus the elements of righteousness in society are: scholars who plan, and rulers who execute and manage affairs. The word hakim (ruler) is derived from hikmah (wisdom) (with a fatha), which is the bridle that restrains the horse and directs it.

Therefore a noble hadith states: "Whoever appoints a man over a group while among the people there is someone better than him, he will not smell the fragrance of the Garden" (4).

Why? Because that spreads corruption in the earth, and weakens lofty resolves and strong aspirations when one sees someone less competent than oneself holding the matter while one is set aside. But when the scale is balanced, each of us will strive to reach his proper place.

Therefore: the task of rulers and holders of authority is the advancement of society. We do not say to a ruler, for example, "Prepare food for us" or "Make a machine for us"; this is not his task. We saw one of the amirs who had land that he cultivated, and an official managed it, whom they called al-Khuwli, whose task was supervision and oversight.

One day the amir came to inspect his land and check its condition in the company of al-Khuwli. During their tour of the land, al-Khuwli saw a channel from which water was flowing until it flooded the crops, so he dismounted and blocked the channel with his own hands.

Thereupon the amir became angry and dismissed him from his post, because he had worked with his own hand while his task was supervision, and he had workers who could do such work.

But why this view in the management of affairs? They said: because if you work with your hand, you are one person; but if you supervise, you can oversee thousands of workers. From here came the matter of specialization in work.

The ruler and holder of authority must uphold the method of Allah and follow up on people's application of it, standing against any corruption, restraining its perpetrator, and rewarding the diligent worker, as the Exalted says in the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn:

﴿He said, "As for one who wrongs, we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment. But as for one who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best, and we will speak to him of our command with ease."﴾ (18:87–88).

This is because Allah, the Exalted, restrains with authority what He does not restrain with the Qur'an. If we left the people of corruption and deviance to the recompense of the Day of Judgment, society would be corrupted. There must be a force that protects the righteousness of society and strikes the hands of the corrupters. There must be a force that prevents those who dare against us and demand the change of our Islamic order.

Therefore He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy...﴾ (8:60). It must be known to the enemy that you possess the deterrent that restrains him if he transgresses against you or attempts to corrupt the righteousness of society.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) says in a hadith (5) that the arrow shot in the cause of Allah gives a share of reward to everyone who took part in preparing and shooting it: the one who cut it from the tree, the one who shaped it, the one who put it on the bow and shot it, because in that is the preservation of the truth and the preservation of righteousness so that it endures and no one corrupts it.

The responsibility here is not limited to rulers and holders of authority; rather, it is the responsibility of every individual regarding whoever is entrusted with any matter of the Muslims, as the hadith states: "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock: the ruler over the people is a shepherd and is responsible for his subjects; a man is a shepherd over his household and is responsible for them; a woman is a shepherdess over her husband's house and children and is responsible for them; a servant is a shepherd over his master's property and is responsible for it. Indeed, each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock" (6).

The worker should not look only to the supervision of the employer; let him be a watchman over himself. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, observes everyone. And there is a sacred hadith: "If you believe that I do not see you, then the defect is in your faith; and if you believe that I see you, why have you made Me the most insignificant of those you look at?"

Whoever reflects on the movement of life finds it interlinked. For example, if you want to build a house, the engineering is a movement, the construction is a movement, the electricity is a movement, the carpentry is a movement, and so on. If we say that this work consists of, for instance, a hundred movements, you possess only one of them, which is your work that you master, and the rest are movements of others. If you are sincere in what people have entrusted to you, Allah will inspire them to be sincere to you, even unintentionally. You were sincere and perfected one movement, and people were sincere to you in ninety-nine movements.

Know that thoughts and ideas are in the hand of Allah, the Exalted. If you watch over Allah in what people have entrusted to you, Allah will watch over them for you in what you have entrusted to them, and He will spare you the burden of watching. A craftsman may make something for you and intend to cheat you in it, but Allah prevents him from this: perhaps one of his acquaintances sits with him and he is ashamed to cheat in front of him, or he does not find the material with which to cheat you, or other causes that Allah subjects for you; so the craftsman perfects his craft for you, even against his will.

Therefore: if you want your affairs to be righteous, set right the affairs of others.

Among the fundamentals by which we set things right and inherit the earth is that we look at all people as equals, with no one having merit over another except through piety and righteous deeds. None of us is a son of Allah, and none of us has a kinship with Allah. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ (49:13).

Islam recognizes no class distinction except in excellence of work: the worth of every person is what he does well. We have given an example of this, and we will mention it even though it concerns a non-Muslim man: he was a French man who was a union leader for the workers, defending their rights and seeking increases in their income from the ministry's budget. When he assumed the office of minister and bore responsibility, he changed what he had been demanding, so the workers protested, and one of them wanted to provoke him and said: "Remember, O Your Excellency the Minister, that one day you were a shoe-shiner." The man replied only: "Yes... but I used to do it well."

We have previously mentioned that Allah, the Exalted, distributed talents and abilities among His creatures. So when you see yourself as distinguished over others in something, do not be deceived by it, and look at what others are distinguished by that you are not. For we are all equal before Allah, and no one is favored over another. You are distinguished by your knowledge or your strength, and others are distinguished by their happiness with their family, or their trustworthiness and the trust people place in them, or their contentment with what has been apportioned to them, or their capacity to restrain themselves and their contentment with little. One of us may be distinguished by a righteous son who is obedient to his father and a delight to his eyes.

Therefore: this is a measured and calculated matter, because

1 Al-Zabur and al-kitab are one (the same), which is why the Torah and the Gospel may be called zabur. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-Zabur is the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4529).
2 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4530): "The best that has been said about it is that it means the earth of Paradise, as Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, because the earth of this world has been inherited by the righteous and others. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others."
3 From Ibn 'Abbas: it is the land of the disbelieving nations, which the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) will inherit through conquests (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4530).
4 From Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever holds any authority over the affairs of the Muslims and appoints someone over them out of favoritism, upon him is the curse of Allah; Allah will not accept from him any exchange or justice until He admits him into Hell." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/6).
5 From 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, admits three people into the Garden by one arrow: its maker who seeks reward in its making, the one who supplies it, and the one who shoots it." Narrated by al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/204), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1637), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2811).
6 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1829) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/111, 54), and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2409).

The message: the important matter that people must know. Therefore, when people are preoccupied with war and await its news arriving in the form of communiqués, they say: "Communiqué number one," because it is an important matter.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 106]: that is, what the Qur'an has brought is the true message, the supreme message, which leaves you no excuse, leaves your heedlessness no room, and leaves no one able to find fault with it in anything. It is the ultimate of what I can inform you of.

And for whom is this message? ﴿For a people who worship.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 106]: that is, those who eagerly receive the will of God to carry it out, whether it is a command or a prohibition.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 107:

Since (ﷺ) is the Seal of the Messengers, and his mission is to all mankind and to all of time until the Hour arrives. The messengers before him were sent for a specific period of time and to specific peoples, but the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) came as a mercy to all the worlds. Therefore it must be able to encompass all the affairs of life that you are living through, that those after you live through, and until the Day of Resurrection.

The meaning of "al-'alamin" (the worlds) is everything other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic: the world of the angels, the world of the jinn, the world of humankind, the world of inanimate matter, the world of animals, and the world of plants. But how can the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) be a mercy to all of them?

They said: Yes, a mercy to the angels. Gabriel (peace be upon him) used to fear the outcome until there was revealed to Muhammad the words of the Exalted: ﴿Possessed of power, with the Lord of the Throne, firmly established﴾ [At-Takwir]. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) was reassured and felt secure.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a mercy to inanimate matter, because he commanded us to remove harmful things from the road. He is also a mercy to animals. In the noble hadith: "No Muslim plants a plant or sows a seed, and then a bird or a person or an animal eats from it, except that it is written for him as a charity" (1).

There is also the hadith of the woman who entered the Fire because of a cat she confined: she neither fed it nor gave it water, nor did she leave it to eat from the vermin of the earth (2).

And the hadith of the man who entered Paradise because he gave water to a dog that was panting and eating moist earth from thirst. The man went down into the well, filled his leather sock, and gave the dog to drink, so Allah thanked him and forgave him, because he went down into the well with no vessel to draw water with, so he devised a way and exerted himself to give the dog water (3).

Thus the mercy of Islam reached animals, birds and humans alike. In the religion there is a principle and a method that organizes everything and leaves no small or great matter in people's lives unregulated, and therefore it is a mercy to the worlds.

So the words of the Exalted: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [Al-Anbiya]: meaning that everything that Islam brings falls within the elements of mercy.

1 A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2320), and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (1553), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him).

2 From Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman entered the Fire because of a cat she tied up; she neither fed it nor let it eat from the vermin of the earth." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (8/33). Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (6/357): "What is meant by 'vermin of the earth' (khashsh al-ard) is the creeping things and insects of the earth, such as mice and the like."

3 From Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "While a man was walking along a road, he became extremely thirsty. He found a well, went down into it and drank, then came out and found a dog panting and eating moist earth from thirst. The man said: 'This dog has reached the same level of thirst that I had reached.' So he went down into the well, filled his sock, held it in his mouth, and gave the dog to drink. Allah thanked him for that and forgave him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a reward for us in (caring for) animals?" He said: "There is a reward for (caring for) every creature with a moist liver." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6009).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 108:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God. So will you submit?"﴾

Oneness (wahdaniyyah) is the first mercy upon us: that we are all equal, having no god but one God. This is among the greatest of God's mercies, that we worship Him alone, without partner. Worshipping Him suffices us from worshipping other than Him. Had there been many gods, we would be bewildered between a god who commands and a god who forbids.

Therefore, the Truthful, may He be exalted, asks us to take pride and honour in this oneness and this divinity. On this, the Islamic poet Muhammad Iqbal says: "And the prostration that you disdain among a thousand prostrations, in it is salvation."

Your prostration to God, and the rubbing of your face in the dust before Him, the Glorified, protects you from prostrating to other than Him. Were it not for your prostration to God, you would prostrate to everyone stronger than you. So you ought to take pride in your servitude to God, for it protects you from servitude to others among mankind, so that no one can say to you, "You are a slave." Yes, I am a slave, but I am not your slave, for the slave of another is free like you.

The Truthful, may He be exalted, has also set us an example on this matter in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿God sets forth a parable: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ [Az-Zumar].

Can a slave to several masters who pull him at the same time, and who are moreover at odds with one another, be equal to a slave wholly devoted to one master?

Thus, we are all slaves of God, Mighty and Majestic. When we submit, we submit only to Him, the Glorified. I do not submit to you, nor do you submit to me. Therefore they say: "The one who is bound by the Law cuts off his finger and no blood flows," because it is a command from above, from heaven, in which no one has any part.

Therefore, servitude is hateful when it is servitude to humans, because in human servitude the master takes the best of his servant; whereas in servitude to God, the servant takes the best of his Master.

And the poet says:
"Enough honour for my self that I am a slave, who is welcomed without appointments.
His Lord, in His most Mighty holiness, but I meet whenever and wherever I love."

Compare an audience with one of the great ones of this world with meeting your Lord, Mighty and Majestic. If you wish to enter upon one of these people, you must request an audience, and who knows whether it will be accepted or refused; and if it is accepted, you possess none of its elements: the time, the place, and the subject of conversation are all matters determined by someone other than you.

As for meeting your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, you need only perform ablution, raise your hands, and say, "God is greater." After that you will be in the presence of God, and you have chosen the time, the place, the subject of discourse, and the ending of the meeting.

Do you not see how God, Exalted, bestowed favour upon His Messenger on the journey of "the Night Journey and the Ascension," by describing him as His servant, saying: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night...﴾ [Al-Isra']? So His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God..."﴾ [Al-Anbiya'] came after His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 107], to show us that God's call to us to worship one God frees us from our servitude to one another.

Then the Truthful, may He be exalted, makes us desirous of this servitude, saying: ﴿So will you submit?﴾ [Al-Anbiya']. Like a parent urging a lazy child to be like his classmate who excelled and took first place, saying, "Will you not study and strive so that you become like him?"

Thus, in ﴿So will you submit?﴾ [Al-Anbiya'], that is: submit to God, for your interest lies in Islam, and your honour lies in your servitude to God.

¹ From the poetry of the Shaykh, may God be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 109:

﴿But if they turn away...﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109]: meaning, they turn away and withdraw.

﴿Then say: "I have announced to you..."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109]. The root is ʾ-dh-n (أذن), from which comes the word adhan (الأذان), meaning the announcing of something. The original sense of announcing was through the ear, by speech, since they had no reading and writing; so announcing depended on speech and hearing by the ear. Thus the meaning of "ādhantukum" (آذنتكم) is: I informed you and notified you.

As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿on equal terms﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109]: meaning, the announcement came to you all together; I did not single out one of you over another. You are equal in the announcement; none of you is distinguished above another. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) was eager to convey to everyone, and he would say:

{May God make radiant the face of a man who hears my saying, understands it, and then conveys it to one who has not heard it, for many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who understands it better than he who heard it themselves.} (1) Thus good is spread and circulated among all.

﴿Then say: "I have announced to you on equal terms"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109]: so I have not informed one people and withheld it from another, nor have I told one ear and not another, and I have made it part of the perfection of faith that the hearer informs the one who has not heard, for none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

Then He alerts them to the matter of the Hour: ﴿And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾ [al-Anbiya': 109]: so be watchful, take heed, and be on your guard, for I do not know; perhaps the Hour will be near, and perhaps it will overtake you before I finish speaking with you.

Therefore, when some righteous man was asked, "How did you spend your life?" he said: "I have spent my life in four matters: I knew that I am never free from the gaze of God for the blink of an eye, so I felt shame before Him to disobey Him; I knew that I have a provision that will not pass me by, which God has guaranteed for me, so I was content with it; I knew that I have a debt that no one else will pay on my behalf, so I busied myself with it; and I knew that I have a term that hastens toward me, so I hastened toward it."

So the meaning is: prepare for this matter before it overtakes you.

1. Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/437), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2658, 2657), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (232), and al-Humaydi in his Musnad (1/47), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud, and He knows what you conceal.﴾ (21:110)

Since your Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows what is spoken aloud and knows the secret and what is more hidden, then beware of being hypocritical. For We forbid you from hypocrisy with people, so it is all the more fitting that We forbid you from being hypocritical toward your Lord, glorified is He, who knows your secret as He knows your openness. The utmost that people can do is to watch your outward conduct. Therefore, all the precautions of the criminals are to hide from the eyes of the state and to flee the surveillance of the police, but how can one hide from the sight and knowledge of God?

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud, and He knows what you conceal﴾ [al-Anbiya']: He teaches us good manners even in what we conceal, so good manners in what is spoken aloud are all the more fitting. We believe that Allah, glorified is He, is the Unseen who is not witnessed, and suppose that you know everything in your house, because it is visible to you; but what is outside the house is unseen to you, which you do not know. As for the Truth, glorified is He, He is the Unseen who knows every visible thing and every unseen thing.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time.﴾ (21:111)

That is: perhaps the respite and your remaining without punishment, and the delay of the Hour from you, is a trial and a test, [and] I wonder whether you will be guided and succeed in this test. As He, glorified is He, said in another place:

﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah intends only to punish them thereby in the worldly life and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 55]

And the Exalted said: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is better for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 178]

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and an enjoyment for a time﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 111]: that is, this bounty and this enjoyment will not last, because it has a appointed term.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 21, verse 112:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) says at the conclusion of Surat al-Anbiya':

﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One sought for help against what you describe."﴾ (112)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth..."﴾ (112) [al-Anbiya']: as the prophets before him had supplicated with this, ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of deciders.﴾ (89) [al-A'raf].

Does God, glorified is He, judge other than with truth? They said: God, glorified is He, makes it clear to us, for we have lived in this world and seen much falsehood, so it is as if we are hearing judgment with truth for the first time.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One sought for help against what you describe.﴾ (112) [al-Anbiya'], meaning: the One sought for help against what you commit of wrong in attributing to us madness, or sorcery, etc.

You notice that the Truthful, glorified is He, in the verses of Surat al-Anbiya' spoke of the folding of the heaven like the folding of the scroll for books, then said: ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ (111) [al-Anbiya'], then said: ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth..."﴾ (112) [al-Anbiya'].

All of this is to bring the matter of the Hour and its establishment near to us, and to prepare us to receive Surat al-Hajj.

1 Qatadah said: The prophets used to say, ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth...﴾ (89) [al-A'raf], so the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to say: ﴿My Lord, judge with truth...﴾ (112) [al-Anbiya'], and when he met the enemy he would say, while knowing that he was upon the truth and his enemy upon falsehood, ﴿My Lord, judge with truth...﴾ (112) [al-Anbiya'], meaning: decide by it. Mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (6/4532) and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/689), who attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim.

2 That is: give us victory over them. It is also possible that the meaning is: "Our Lord, open between us and our people the door of mutual understanding and love in truth, until they believe and abandon their obstinacy." [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/70].

3 Said by Ibn 'Abbas, as transmitted from him by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and Ibn al-Mundhir, cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/689), who said: God does not judge except with truth, but he [the Prophet] only hastens toward that in this world, asking his Lord concerning his people.
